title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Agni, come hither for our enjoyment, praised as you are, for the giving of oblations. Sit down, O priest, upon the sacred grass; you, O Agni, are the invoking priest of all sacrifices, placed here for the good.
Among human beings, through the gods.
We choose Agni as our messenger, as the invoking priest who knows all, the wise performer of this sacrifice.
Agni, bright and kindled, fed with offerings, strikes down all obstructions, longing for riches, with his wondrous power.
I praise your most beloved guest, dear as a friend — O Agni, like a chariot worthy of being known.
O Agni, with your great powers protect us from all ill will, and also from the hatred of mortal men.
Come, O Agni, let me now speak to you; these other hymns are here for you. Wax mighty with these Soma drops.
The calf draws your mind even from the highest resting place, O Agni; I desire you with my song.
O Agni, Atharvan rubbed you forth from the lotus blossom, from the head of every worshipping priest.
O Agni, bring us, like Vivasvat, great aid for our protection; for you are truly a god for us to behold.
Crush the ungenerous enemy.
Him who knows all, the immortal carrier of oblations, the most excellent sacrificer — you adorn your messenger with a hymn.
The related hymns, pointing toward you, prepared with oblations, have taken their stand in the presence of Vāyu.
O Agni, day by day, at dawn and dusk, we come to you with our thoughts, bringing homage.
O Ancient Awakener, distinguish this — for every clan, for the one worthy of worship — the hymn of praise, visible to Rudra.
You are invoked for the protection of that beautiful, faultless sacrifice. Come, O Agni, with the Maruts.
We would honor you, O Agni, with obeisances, like a horse with a mane — you who reign over all sacrifices.
Like Aurva and Bhṛgu, I call upon the bright one, like Apnavāna — Agni, clothed in the ocean.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The mortal who kindles Agni with his mind and thought accompanies the divine. I kindle Agni with the rays of the sun.
Then men behold the light, born of the ancient seed, as the day dawns — when it blazes far away in the sky.
Toward the mighty grandson.
May Agni with his sharp flame extend all-pervading, consuming every devourer. May Agni win riches for us.
O Agni, be gracious; you are great — come to the god-loving people. You have approached to take your seat on the sacred grass.
O Agni, O god, guard us from sin, ward off those who would harm us. With your fiercest flames, burn them, O ageless one.
O Agni, O god, yoke your swift steeds, those that are good and noble. The swift ones carry well.
We place you, O lord of the tribe, the brilliant one, O Agni fed with oblations, to grant us brave heroes.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of the earth. He quickens the seeds of the waters.
Do proclaim, O Agni, this our fresh Gāyatra gain, newly composed, among the gods.
Gopavana gave you birth with his song, O Agni, O Aṅgiras. You, the purifier — hear our invocation.
Agni, the lord of nourishment, the wise one, has stridden around the oblations, bestowing gems upon the worshipper.
The rays carry aloft that divine Jātavedas — the sun — to be seen by all the world.
Praise the wise Agni, the upholder of truth in the sacrifice, the god who drives away disease.
May the divine waters be auspicious for our protection, auspicious for our drinking. May they flow toward us bringing welfare and healing.
Whose thoughts do you now encompass and quicken, O lord of the good? Whose hymns do you delight in?
Let us sing forth the immortal Jātavedas, the beloved, as one praises a dear friend.
Protect us, O Agni, with one hymn; protect us also with a second. Protect us, O lord of strength, with three hymns; protect us, O generous one, with four.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Agni, O god, with your great flames and brilliant radiance, kindled for Bharadvāja, O youngest one, O purifier rich in gifts — shine forth.
In you, O Agni, well-fed with oblations, may the worshippers be beloved — those lords of bounty who govern the people and share out the pen of cattle.
O Agni, praised singer, lord of the tribe, scorching the demons, O god — you, the tireless lord of the house, are great, the guardian of heaven, dwelling in the hall.
O Agni, like Vivasvat, the bright reward of the dawns, O immortal, O Jātavedas — bring today the gods to the worshipper, you who rise with the dawn.
O bright one, O generous one, with your wonderful aid urge on the gifts. O Agni, you are the charioteer of these riches; find us a firm footing and a safe path for us.
You alone, O Agni, have this fame — guardian of the cosmic order, wise one. The inspired sages, the creators of wisdom, kindle you bright and seek your favor.
O Agni, O purifier, bring us riches that augment our strength, worthy of praise. And grant us, O matchless one, wealth longed for by many, with good guidance, bringing greater glory.
He who distributes all goods, the cheerful invoking priest of the people — as honey fills the first cups, let praises flow to Agni.
The most beloved, the most perceptive one, the minister of the perfect sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
You rest in the forests, among the mothers; the mortals kindle you together. Untiring, you carry the oblation, O receiver of offerings, and then you reign among the gods.
He has been seen, the best knower of the way, in whom they have placed their vows. May our hymns go forth to Agni, born and nourished, the increaser of the noble.
Agni is the household priest established in the hymn; the pressing stones and sacred grass are in the sacrifice. With a verse I invoke the Maruts, Brahmaṇaspati, and the gods — the most excellent protection.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Praise Agni with hymns for protection, him of the sharp flame. Praise Agni for wealth, O much-praised one; O men, the celebrated Agni is a shelter for brilliant shining.
Hear, O Agni of the heard ear, with the gods who bear offerings and who travel together. Let Mitra and Aryaman take their seat on the sacred grass at the sacrifice with those who travel at dawn.
Agni, the son of the divine gift, blazes forth like the god Indra in his greatness. He has turned after his mother Earth and stood in the shelter of heaven's vault.
From the earth or from the bright expanse of the vast heaven — grow with this body and this hymn of mine; fulfil what has been born, O Agni of good understanding.
Blazing, you went through the forests when you reached your mothers, the waters. I shall not forget your turning back, O Agni, though you were far away and yet came close.
Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for people for all time. You shine, O Kaṇva; born of cosmic order, nourished, you are the one whom the peoples revere.
Let the god who gives wealth wish for you a full ladle. Pour it out upward or fill it up — then the god will carry you forward.
Let Brahmaṇaspati go forward; let the divine, joyful word go forward. May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the heroic, manly, bountiful one, the lord of the fivefold verse.
Stand upright for our help, like the god Savitṛ. Stand upright to win the prize when we invoke you with anointed worshippers.
The mortal who desires to lead toward wealth, who worships you, O Vasu — he gains a hero, O Agni, a reciter of hymns, a nourisher of thousands by his own power.
We choose for you the great Agni of the many peoples, of the clans devoted to the gods — with well-spoken words and hymns — him whom no other kindles at the same time.
This Agni is master of heroic valor and of good fortune. He is master of wealth with fine offspring, master of riches with cattle, master of the slaying of Vṛtra.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You, O Agni, are the lord of the house; you are the Hotṛ priest at our sacrifice. You are the Potar, all-desired, all-knowing — you cut through and also win what is desirable.
We mortals have chosen you, the god, as a friend for help — child of the waters, bringer of good fortune, rich in fine deeds, with excellent swiftness, without blemish.
At the seat of Iḷā, with reverence and with offerings freely given, worship the adorable lord of the homesteads.
Wondrous is the swelling of the young sprouting one, like one who follows the two mothers to give suck. When he was born without a teat yet he grew strong — at once he goes performing his great mission.
This one light is yours, and another beyond — enter in union with the third light. Being a dweller together, become beautiful in body; be dear to the gods at the highest birthplace.
Let us fashion this hymn of praise for worthy Jātavedas, like a chariot, with intelligence. For blessed is the guidance of this one in his assembly — O Agni, may we not be harmed in your friendship.
Agni Vaiśvānara, the head of heaven, the pillar of the earth, born of cosmic order — the gods who were near generated the vessel: the wise one, the sovereign, the guest of peoples.
The gods generated you with hymns, O Agni, like waters from the back of a mountain. The well-praised songs speed you to win the prize — as prize-bearing horses have won a race.
Make Agni, the Rudra of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ who truly sacrifices for the two worlds, the gold-formed one — make him your refuge, before the unnoticed thunder, for help.
The lord, the mortal's own, is kindled with reverences, whose face is poured with ghee. Men praise him with offerings together in pressing — Agni shines at the forefront of the dawns.
Agni goes forth with his great banner; the bull roars as he fills both worlds. He has lifted up what is highest even from the end of heaven; the great buffalo has grown in the lap of the waters.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Men have generated the praised Agni, hidden in the two fire-sticks, with their thoughts — seen from afar, the lord of the house, the unwearied one.
Like great birds spreading their wings upward, his rays stream forth toward the vault of heaven.
Proclaim the great conquering one, the widely inspiring, the wise among the unwise, the breaker of strongholds — lead him with hymns through the forests; fix thought — he who shines with yellow beard like one clad in armor, brilliant with wealth.
One of your faces is bright, another is adorable — you are like heaven with your two differently-formed days. For you, self-sustaining one, protect all magic arts — may your bountiful gift be here, O Pūṣan.
O Agni, accomplish for the one who calls the refreshing, much-wondrous winning of cows, ever-lasting. May there be for us a son, an offspring bearing descendants — O Agni, may that gracious thought of yours be for us.
The Hotṛ, being born great, has pierced heaven; the man-seated one has taken his place in the expanse of waters. He who placed himself at the pressed soma dispenses vigor — he who guides riches to the worshipper is a protector of bodies.
Let the praising doors wish forward the sovereign, the praised one of the asura power, the laudable male of the peoples — let them wish forward the heroic deeds done, as those of Indra.
Jātavedas is hidden in the two fire-sticks, like an embryo well carried by pregnant mothers. Agni is to be praised day by day by the wakeful, the offering-bearing human beings.
From of old, O Agni, you crush the sorcerers; the demons have not conquered you in battles. Burn them along with the stupid ones, the flesh-eaters — may they not escape from your divine weapon.
Speed for us the path to most praiseworthy wealth, to the prize.
If a hero were to follow and a mortal were to kindle Agni — pouring the offering continually, he would enjoy the divine shelter.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Your impetuous smoke moves in heaven, blazing bright and spread wide. For you, O Pāvaka, shine with splendor like the sun, with radiance.
You, O Agni, possess fame like a ruler; you govern like Mitra. You, the wide-seeing one, O Vasu, nourish renown as one nourishes prosperity.
In the morning, Agni, the much-beloved guest, should be praised throughout the settlements — he in whom, the immortal, mortals kindle the offering.
What is most to be borne — that goes to Agni of the great hymn, the widely-shining one. Like a great cow, wealth springs from you; prizes spring from you.
Striving for the prize, I praise Agni, the much-loved guest of each and every clan, with the thoughts of the powerful hymn — for you, the praise worthy of a house.
With a great swelling hymn of praise to the divine Agni of the light — him whom mortals have placed in front for praise, like a Mitra.
We have come to the most Vṛtra-slaying, the greatest, the human Agni — who, the famous one, is kindled in the Nārkṣa asterism with a great visage.
Born by the higher law, when he came into being together with those who grow together — when Agni was the father of Kaśyapa, Faith was the mother, Manu the sage.
Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahmā, and Bṛhaspati —
From here they rose up, climbing the back of heaven, climbing upward. Like the many victorious ones, along the path, the Aṅgirases traveled to the sky.
O Agni, we kindle you for great wealth, for gift-giving. Praise the great bull for the great priestly calling — heaven and earth.
He runs forward when one speaks the word 'brahman' to him — they call it that. He has gone around all poetic wisdom like the felly of a wheel.
O Agni, with your flame strike flame, hear from all around — bend down and break the strength, the might, of the sorcerer demon.
You, O Agni, sacrifice here to the Vasus, to the Rudras, and to the Ādityas. Sacrifice for the people of the perfect rite, the people born of Manu, those who sprinkle ghee.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
I, ever-giving, call upon you much, O Agni — truly yours. Like a refuge from the sharp thorn, you are a shelter of greatness.
Carry forth the ancient word, great and primal, to Agni the Hotṛ. Like a sage bearing the lights of the waters, he is the wise ordainer.
O Agni, lord of wealth rich in cattle, O son of strength — grant to us, O Jātavedas, great renown.
O Agni, most worthy of worship at the rite, sacrifice to the gods for the god-seeking worshipper. The Hotṛ, gladdening, shines forth, dispelling failures.
Born, he sought wisdom from the seven mothers for glory. This one, firm and steadfast among riches, became discerning.
And may this thought of ours, Aditi, come to us by day with her aid. May she, bringing peace, grant us delight and drive away failures.
Praise him indeed, worship Jātavedas who faces all directions — whose smoke moves freely, whose flame cannot be grasped.
No mortal foe can overcome him, whether by craft or cunning, who has given offering to Agni, the receiver of oblations.
Drive away that crooked foe, that thief, O Agni, that ill-minded one. Make the path easy, far away from him, O lord of the good.
Hear, O Agni, my new hymn of praise, O hero, lord of peoples. Burn down with your heat the deceitful demons.
Praises go up to Agni.
He, O Agni, crosses over with your aids, with good heroes, with prize-winning deeds — he whose friendship you have cherished.
Honour him, the swift golden one; the gods have sent the divine messenger onward. You carry the oblation to the gods.
Let not Agni, the wealth-giving guest, much-praised and ruling, be wrathful with us — he who is the good Hotṛ, the one of excellent rites.
Auspicious is Agni when invoked for us, auspicious is his gift, O blessed one; auspicious is the rite, and auspicious too are the praises.
We have chosen you, most worthy of worship, divine Hotṛ among the gods, immortal — of good purpose for this sacrifice.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Agni, bring that splendour which, conquering all, sits in the abode, overcoming every devourer — the wrath of the ill-minded among people.
Or when the lord of the clan, sharp and well-pleased, guards the tribe of Manu — then Agni of all things repels the demons.
Sing that for him, when the Soma is pressed, together, to the much-invoked hero — as a blessing, like to the able bull for the cow.
That rapture of yours, O Indra of a hundred powers, which is most radiant — with that rapture exhilarate us now.
The cows low near the great trough, the prize-giver of the sacrifice, with both its golden ears.
Sing fittingly for the horse, for the famous one of the shoulder-strap, and for the cow — fittingly for the dwelling of Indra.
We speed on Indra, great for the slaying of Vṛtra. May he be the bull, the virile one.
You, O Indra, were born above strength, from might and vigour. You, winning as a bull, are the bull indeed.
The sacrifice strengthened Indra when he rolled back the earth and made an attachment in the sky.
O Indra, if I were as you, the sole lord of wealth — then my singer would be the companion of my cattle.
O pressers, hasten again and again, worthy of praise, for the exhilarating drink — Soma for the hero, for the champion.
O Vasu, drink this pressed Soma-juice with a well-filled belly. We have granted it to you without fear.
You travel, O Sun, as the unsetting one.
Whatever you rise over today, O Vṛtra-slayer, O Sun shining upon all — all that, O Indra, is under your will.
He who led Turvaśa and Yadu from the distant land with good guidance — that Indra is our ever-young companion.
O Indra, let not the sun restrain us from any direction in the night. With you as ally may we win that.
O Indra, bring the winning wealth, conquering and ever-victorious, the most abundant, for our aid.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
We call upon Indra in the great battle for great wealth, and Indra in the small — the thunderbolt-wielder, the yoke-fellow in conflicts.
Indra drank the pressed Soma of the Kadrū plant at the thousand-armed one's feast. There he declared his heroic might.
We who desire you, O Indra, call out to you again and again, O bull. Know yourself as ours, O lord of wealth.
Those who kindle Agni and strew the sacred grass in order — Indra is the ever-young companion of such men.
Break all enmities, repel the pressures on every side, slay the scorners. Then bring the desirable wealth.
They adorn the wondrous path downward.
These Soma-pressing companions gaze upon you, O Indra — as those rich in cattle watch over the animal.
Before the wrath of that one, all peoples and all tribes bow down — as rivers bow to the ocean.
The great help of the gods — that we choose for ourselves; the aid of the bountiful bulls, for our protection.
Make the Soma-cups resound, O Lord of Prayer. May the Auśija, he of the armpit, Kakṣīvant, be your Soma-drinker.
Let the Vṛtra-slayer of many pressings be alert in mind for us. May the mighty Śakra hear the blessing.
O divine Savitṛ, today impel auspicious fortune for us together with progeny. Drive away ill dreams.
Where is this young bull, thick-necked and unbowing? What Brahmin priest serves him with devotion?
In the hidden place of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers, the wise one was born through inspired thought.
Let the praiser sing forth, with fresh songs, Indra the sovereign of all peoples, the hero, the vanquisher of men, the most bountiful.
He drank with his jaw the Soma juice of him of beautiful jaw, the well-skilled one who pours offerings — Indra indeed is Indra, the barley-mixed.
These songs, O Wealthy One, resound toward you in praise — like milch-cows lowing toward their calf.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Here indeed they found the secret name of the cow belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ — thus in the house of the Moon.
When Indra, unhindered and most showering, led forth the great waters, there Pūṣan was present at his side.
The shining cow gives suck — she who is glory-seeking, the mother of the Maruts, the generous ones, harnessed as the bearer of the chariots.
Come to us with your tawny steeds to the pressed soma, O Lord of raptures — come to us with your tawny steeds to the pressed soma.
The desired priestly libations have been poured forth, magnifying Indra at the rite — toward the concluding bath with vigor.
I alone have grasped from the Father the wisdom of immortality — I was born like the sun.
Let our joint festival-joys in Indra be rich, abundantly strong — rich in wealth, by which we may rejoice.
Soma and Pūṣan, perceivers of all good dwellings, are yoked as charioteers in the divine realm.
The all-conquering, hundred-powered, most bountiful one among men.
Sing forth for Indra the exhilarating hymn, O friends — for the tawny-steeded, soma-drinking one.
We indeed, O Indra, for that very purpose — friends devoted to you — the Kaṇvas grow old praising you with recitations.
For Indra, for his exhilaration, let our songs resound around the pressed soma — let the singers worship with the hymn.
This soma of yours, O Indra, is purified upon the sacred grass — come, hasten here, drink of it.
For aid we invoke the beautiful craftsman, as a milker milks a good-milking cow — day by day we call.
O Bull, toward you I pour the pressed soma upon the pressing-stones for your drinking — be satisfied, spread your exhilaration wide.
The soma that is poured for you, O Indra, in the cups and in the vessels — you are the lord over drinking of it.
At each yoking we call upon the most powerful, at each prize-contest — friends calling Indra for his aid.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Come here, sit down, and sing forth to Indra — O friends who bring the hymns of praise.
Drink, O you who are delighted by songs.
Great is Indra, and before us too let greatness belong to the thunderbolt-bearer — his might is broad like the sky.
Come now, O Indra, seize and gather for us the splendid, wealth-rich prize — with your great right hand.
Praise and sing forth to Indra the lord of the mountain-cows as you know him — the son of Truth, the true lord.
By what means shall the wondrous one, the ever-growing friend, come to us in aid — accompanied by what most powerful deed?
That altogether-conquering one, stretched forth in all your songs — set him in motion for your aid.
For the wonderful lord of the assembly hall, the dear and beloved one of Indra, I have sought the winning of wisdom.
Those paths of yours that are beneath the sky, by which you sent forth Vyaśva — may the worlds hear us too.
Bring to us blessings upon blessings, food and strength, O Hundred-powered — when you, O Indra, show us grace.
This soma has been pressed — the Maruts drink of it, and likewise the self-ruling Aśvins.
Winning for themselves great heroic strength.
We do not diminish the gods, we do not obstruct anything — we walk in the hearing of sacred utterance.
Evening has come — sing the great song, the bright song, O descendant of Atharvan — praise the god Savitṛ.
This Dawn, unprecedented, the dear one of the sky, shines forth — I praise the two lovely Aśvins greatly.
Indra, unapproachable, with the bones of Dadhīca smote the obstacles — ninety-nine he slew.
Come, O Indra, exhilarate yourself with all the soma-pressings — the great one, powerful in conquest.
Come, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, come to our side — the great one with great aids.
His might gleams in that — when he rolled both together, Indra spread the two worlds apart like a hide.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
This one is like a pigeon carrying an embryo toward you, O equal one — do you not carry that speech for us?
May the Wind blow its medicine, bringing peace and joy to our heart — may it extend our life-spans for us.
That person is not deceived by anyone.
As before with cattle, with horses, and with chariots — honor us with the bounty of the great ones.
These dappled cows of yours, O Indra, milk clarified butter mixed with milk — swollen full with the immortal.
By this thought and by the prayer for cattle, O much-named, much-praised one — when you, O Soma, arose as Soma.
May Sarasvatī, pure, rich in nourishment, possessing strength — she who is wealthy in prayer — desire our sacrifice.
Who among the Nahuṣa-folk would satisfy Indra here with soma? Let him bring us riches.
Come here — for the way is good for you, O Indra — drink this soma; this sacred grass is my seat.
Great and lowest among the three, gleaming in the sky — the might of Mitra and Aryaman, and the unconquerable power of Varuṇa.
We, O Indra, O much-wealthy one, O guide, are yours — we stand as holders of your tawny steeds.
May the somas gladden you, O wielder of the stone; bestow your bounty. Strike down the enemies of sacred speech.
O lover of hymns, protect our pressed soma; you are anointed with streams of sweetness. Indra, glory comes only from your gift.
Indra has always been drawing you near and attending upon you duly. No god is chosen over valiant Indra.
May the soma drops enter you as rivers flow into the ocean. No one surpasses you, O Indra.
The singers praise Indra loudly, the chanters praise Indra with their hymns. The melodies have celebrated Indra.
May Indra give us food, the Ṛbhu-lord grants Ṛbhu-wealth. May the prize-winner give us the prize.
Indra alone has driven away great terror, moving against it. For he is steadfast and far-seeing.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
These songs attend you at each pressing, O lover of hymns, as milch-cows seek their calf.
Let us now call upon Indra and Pūṣan for friendship, for well-being, for the winning of strength.
None is higher than you, O Indra, none is greater, O slayer of Vṛtra. None is like you.
I shall praise him who is the same to all alike.
These praises were released toward you, O Indra; they have joyfully risen up to greet you, the bull, the lord, with one accord.
That mortal is truly well-guided whom the Maruts protect, whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Āspā guard from the treacherous.
Whatever desirable wealth lies in the firm stronghold, whatever is carried off in the rocky place — bring that, O Indra.
We have heard of the greatest slayer of Vṛtra; proclaim the host of peoples for blessing and for great bounty.
May we be equal to winning your glory, O Indra, O hero who wields such power. May we be equal, O Śakra, in your leading forth.
O Indra, delight in us at dawn — in our roasted grain, our groats, our cakes, and our recitations.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you rolled off the head of Namuci, when you conquered all rivals.
These, O Indra, are your pressed somas, and those yet to be pressed. Be gladdened by them, O lord of abundant wealth.
The pressed somas are for you; the sacred grass is spread, O lord of brilliant light. Show grace to your praisers, O Indra.
Pour forth the most generous one with the soma drops.
Come near to us from here, O Indra, with hundredfold strength, with food and thousandfold strength.
The slayer of Vṛtra, newly born, grasped the mace and asked his mother: who are the mighty here, who are heard among them?
We call on the utterer of great hymns, of flowing and streaming songs, for aid — the one who fulfills all goals, for protection.
Varuṇa leads us by straight guidance; Mitra leads us, the wise one; Aryaman, delighting together with the gods.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The red, tawny light, as if coming from far away while standing here, has flashed forth; it has spread its radiance everywhere.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pasture with ghee; you of good resolve, sprinkle the realms with sweetness.
Those sons — the hymns — have stretched toward the highest regions in the sacrifices, resonating and bending their knees to journey forth.
Viṣṇu strode this out; he set down his step threefold. His footstep, shrouded in dust, is gathered together.
At his gifting, drink the pressed soma.
What speech is recited to the great, wise-minded god? That is truly the growth of his fire.
Neither the uktha hymn when recited, nor wealth, nor the snake perceive what is here. Nor is the Gāyatra metre when sung.
Indra is most gladdened by the uktha hymns, lord of prizes and of strengths, possessor of the bay horses, friend of those who press the soma.
Come near to our pressed soma with your prizes; do not be wrathful, like a great man with a young wife.
When, O Vasu, will you be pleased with the praise? Come, halt your chariot — for a long draught of the pressed soma, that you may be satiated as by the wind.
O Indra, drink the soma from the brahmin's bounty, according to the seasons. This friendship with you is inviolable.
We indeed are your praisers, O Indra, O lover of hymns. You, drinker of soma, quicken us.
O Indra, in whatever battles, place manly strength in our bodies. O all-conquering, mighty one — virility.
For you are truly a lover of heroes, and a hero, and steadfast. Your mind is truly one that achieves gifts.
Indra, lord of this moving world, beholding the sun, lord of what stands firm.
You alone we call, O brilliant one, at the winning of the prize. You, O Indra, lord of the good — the warriors call you in battles with Vṛtra; you at the racecourses for horses.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Sing forth to Indra of great bounty, as is fitting. He, the generous one full of wealth, teaches his praisers as if with a thousand gifts.
We proclaim that wonder-worker, conqueror in battle, gladdened with the wealth of soma — as milch-cows call their calf at evening time, so we call Indra with our songs.
With penetrating songs I call Indra, finder of wealth, pressing together for your aid. Singing loudly at the sacrifice where soma is pressed, I call him like a bearer bearing a load.
The swift one truly desires to win the prize, yoked with wisdom. I bend Indra, much-invoked, toward you with my song, as a craftsman bends a well-made wheel-rim.
Drink of the pressed, flavorful soma; be gladdened, O Indra, as with one who possesses cattle. Be our ally in the shared enjoyment and growth; may your thoughts protect us.
Come to the needy one; find him a share, a dwelling of wealth. Pour out your gifts, O generous one, for the winning of cattle, for the winning of horses, O Indra.
Neither does desire regard the last, nor Vasiṣṭha reflect too carefully. Today may all the Maruts, the willing ones, drink together at our soma-pressing.
Speak of nothing else, O friends; suffer no harm. Praise only Indra the bull together at the soma-pressing; again and again recite the uktha hymns.
No one can attain him by action, the one who made the ever-growing — Indra, celebrated everywhere by sacrifices, wise and invincible, bold in his strength.
He who, even without libation, was wounded before through the collar-bones — Maghavan, the generous one, is the joiner of joints, the restorer of what is dislocated.
A thousand, yea a hundred, harnessed to the golden car — let the prayer-yoked, maned bay steeds bring you, O Indra, to drink the soma.
Come, O Indra, with your gladdening bay steeds whose hairs are like peacock-feathers. Let no one hold you back, let no bonds restrain you; pass over them as over a desert and come.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You, the god most mighty, truly do praise the mortal. There is none other than you, O Maghavan, to show mercy — I speak this word to you, O Indra.
You, O Indra, are famed as the straight-pressing lord of strength. You alone slay the obstructing Vṛtras, you who drive forward the unyielding, the upholder of all peoples.
For the divine company we call Indra; we call Indra at the sacrifice being performed; we call Indra in the battle for the spoil; we call Indra for the winning of wealth.
May these praises of mine increase you, O Purūvasas. The bright-toned, pure, and wise ones have sung forth praise-hymns to you.
These sweetest praises and lauds rise up, conquerors of wealth altogether, with inexhaustible bounty, striving for the prize like chariots.
As a wild bull, thirsting, goes to the water that has been gathered not yet drunk — come swiftly to us in the time of drinking and before the feast; among the Kaṇvas drink well in fellowship.
As one follows Bhaga, so we follow you, O hero, glorious and the finder of wealth.
The goods you brought away, O Indra, the heavenly wealth from the asuras — increase the praiser thereof, O Maghavan, and those who have strewn the sacred grass for you.
Sing forth the companionable truth-guarded speech to Mitra and Aryaman; sing the delightful praise, the sheltering hymn, to the royal Varuṇa.
The Āyus who first drank the soma have praised you, O Indra, with hymns; the Ṛbhus, joining their voices together, and the Rudras chant the ancient praises.
O Maruts, sing the mighty prayer to great Indra. The slayer of Vṛtra, the hundred-powered one, smites Vṛtra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
Sing aloud, O Maruts, to Indra the mightiest slayer of Vṛtra — by whom the truth-exalting gods generated the light, the wakeful one for the god's sake.
Bring us wisdom, O Indra, as a father brings to his sons. Instruct us, O much-invoked one, in this journey, that we may live and attain light.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Do not turn away from us, O Indra; be near us in the common feast. You are our help, you are our kinship — do not turn away from us, O Indra.
We who have pressed soma and have strewn the sacred grass sit around you like waters around the pure filter, O Vṛtra-slayer; the praisers attend you.
Whatever strength and manly power you have, O Indra, among the Nahuṣa peoples, or whatever brilliance you have among the five peoples — bring it here; bring all manly powers together.
For you, the mighty bull, are heard in the distant regions; the bull is famed in the near regions.
Whether you are in the far region or in the near, O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śakra — even from there the soma-presser seeks you with hymns, O long-maned Indra, day by day.
Sing with the great hymn to the hero exhilarated by soma-draughts, the all-knowing one — Indra, renowned by name, the mighty one, as a word is heard.
O Indra, grant the triple-seated shelter, the triple-protected refuge for well-being. Grant protection to the Maghavans and to me; ward off the missiles from us.
As all things lean toward the sun, all partake of Indra's bounty. Born with strength through his births, we look toward our share as our due.
No god, no long-lived mortal has attained that power. Even as the swift steed Etaśa is harnessed, so Indra harnesses his two bay steeds.
Adorn Indra, the invocable, in all our battles; approach the prayers and the soma-pressings, O Vṛtra-slayer with highest bow — we have sung our hymn.
Yours indeed, O Indra, is the lowest wealth, yours you nourish the middle; you reign altogether over the highest of all; none bars you in matters of cattle.
Where are you now, where do you stand? For your mind ranges widely. You are roused, O warrior, breaker of the crooked ones, destroyer of citadels — the Gāyatra singers have praised you.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
We have indeed fattened him here, the thunderbolt-bearer. For him therefore bring today at the pressing the pressed soma; truly adorn him who is renowned.
I praise the overcomer of all armies, the mightiest, the slayer of Vṛtra.
From where we fear, O Indra, from there make us fearless. Enable that, O Maghavan, for our protection; smite away enemies, smite away the foes.
O Lord of the homestead, you are the firm pillar, the constant protector of the soma-drinkers. The drop that breaks the everlasting citadels — Indra is the friend of the sages.
Truly you are great, O Sun; truly you are great, O Āditya. Your greatness is wondrous as you exist, O most admirable; by your greatness, O god, you are great.
The one with horses and chariot, of beautiful form, wealthy in cattle — such is your friend, O Indra; he partakes of food shared with dogs and always goes with brilliant companions to the assembly.
If there were a hundred heavens of yours, O Indra, and a hundred earths — a thousand suns could not equal you, O bearer of the thunderbolt; neither could the two worlds that were born encompass you.
Whether you are called eastward or westward, northward or led by men, O Indra — truly you are mighty, born of men; you belong to Anava and to Turvaśa, O foremost of hosts.
What mortal with wealth dares to challenge you, O Indra? For faith in you, O Maghavan, prevails in the farther heaven; the prize-winning steed ever seeks its prize.
This footless one came before those with feet, O Indra and Agni. Having left its head, it has cooked and moved with its tongue, going thirty-footed downward.
Come nearer, O Indra, with measured, wisdom-filled aids. Come with the most beneficial of conquering powers, with the best of sleep-giving gifts.
The swift one, the conqueror, the thrower, the best charioteer, the unhurried one, the increaser of Tugriya — him I praise.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
May the worshippers not cause you to stray far from us. Come from afar to the common feast, or being here, hear us well.
Press out the soma for the soma-drinking, thunderbolt-bearing Indra. Cook the foods for his protection; truly he who gives fills the giver with joy.
We call on Indra, the all-conquering, all-seeing one. O you of a thousand angers, of great might, lord of the good — be our increaser in battles.
O you two who are wealthy in powers, direct your powers to us day and night. May your bounty never fail, and may our gift to you never fail at any time.
Whenever a mortal praiser calls out to the bountiful one, he should approach Varuṇa with inspired speech and voice — Varuṇa, the upholder of those who have gone astray.
Protect the cattle with the intoxication of the soma-juice for Indra, O Medhyātithi — he who is mingled with the two bay steeds, the golden one; Indra, the thunderbolt-bearer, the golden one.
May Indra hear both things and this word of ours spoken here. May Maghavan, the all-conquering one, come with wisdom for the drinking of soma, O mightiest one.
You who hold the stone are not given away from us for a great price, nor for a thousand, nor for ten thousand, O thunderbolt-bearer, nor for a hundred, O you who have hundreds of gifts.
You are better to me than a father and than a brother who does not support; you and my mother delight me equally, O Vasu, for the attainment of wealth.
These soma draughts mixed with curds have been pressed out for Indra. Come to them, O thunderbolt-bearing one, for exhilaration and drinking — come home with your two bay horses.
These soma juices, O Indra, bright and rich in sacred verse, have been pressed for your delight. Having drunk of the sweet, hear our hymns and give bounty to our praise, O lover of song.
Today I call you who are born of the Gāyatrī hymn, you who are like a milch-cow yielding abundance — Indra, the divine milch-cow, another one yielding good milk, whose streams are broad and who is well prepared.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Not the great and solid mountains hold you back, O Indra. When you bestow wealth upon the one who praises you and worships you, no adversary diminishes your gift.
Who knows him drinking companionably at the soma pressing? Who has set him as a twin? He is this one who shatters cities with his strength, who grows exhilarated from the juice that touches his cheeks.
When, O Indra, you drive away from the seat the one who transgresses your command, O Maghavan, place our soma stalk — the one widely coveted — upon the sacrificial grass for the winning of wealth.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati protect our divine speech. May Aditi with her sons and brothers protect us — our speech that is hard to cross and that is our refuge.
Never are you barren, O Indra, and you do not abandon the devout worshipper. O Maghavan, you become ever more abundant — truly, the gift of the divine one is extolled.
Yoke your two bay horses, O Indra, greatest destroyer of Vṛtra, from the distant realm. Come near, O Maghavan, come here with your great steeds to drink the soma, O mighty one.
You indeed, O thunderbolt-bearer, the men of abundant gifts enriched yesterday. So, O Indra, bearer of praise-songs, hear here — come to your own dwelling.
The great waters cover darkness with the eye of sight; the skilled one makes light.
These dawning invocations at daybreak call to you both, O Aśvins. I here invoke you both for help, O you rich in powers — for you go to every clan.
Where are you, O Aśvins? Which mortal burns for you, O gods? Striking with your stony weapon by night, pressing out the soma-stalk — thus indeed you have come to him.
This soma, most rich in sweetness, has been pressed for you both at the heavenly invocations. Drink it, O Aśvins, through the days and nights; bestow treasures upon the devout worshipper.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
I, the bowstring, always seeking you by the stream of soma — I have made the fierce one, like a wild beast, angry at the soma pressings. Who would not entreat the sovereign one?
O Adhvaryu priest, pour out the soma swiftly — Indra thirsts. Now indeed he has yoked his two powerful bay horses and the Vṛtra-slayer has come here.
Bring then what surpasses that, O Indra — the greater beyond the lesser. For you have become Purūvasu, O Maghavan, and you are to be invoked in every battle and every conflict.
O Indra, if I were master of as much as you are master of, I would hold the praiser alone and I would not take delight in evil, O giver of wealth.
You, O Indra, surpass all rivals in swift attacks. You are the slayer of the slanderer, the creator, the swift one who breaks through Vṛtra — you are the swift one who overcomes the attacker.
He who has grown beyond the seats of heaven by his might — no earthly realm has encompassed you, O Indra; you have extended beyond all the universe.
We waken you, O lord of bay horses, with sacrifices; waken, as with a hymn, in the exhilarations of the soma juice.
Your seat, O Indra, has been made ready in the place of sacrifice — come forward thither with the men, O much-invoked one. Be our protector and our increaser; give us riches and be gladdened by the soma.
You burst open the fountains and released their streams; you set free the floods that were bound and confined. When you, O Indra, split open the great mountain and let the streams flow down, when you smote the Dānavas.
We who have pressed the soma, O Indra, praise you hoping to win the prize, O you whose wealth is prominently known. Bring to us good fortune whose shelter we may achieve with our bodies — may we be strengthened by your aid.
We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, longing for wealth, O lord of wealth. For we know you as the bull-lord of cattle, O hero — give us brilliant, bountiful riches.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The men invoke Indra with devoted worship when those prayers that are appointed are yoked. The hero who conquers men, who loves glory — give us a share in the cattle-pen full of cows.
The birds with beautiful wings, the beloved-wisdom sages, calling upon him, have approached Indra. Roll away the darkness, fill the eye with sight, release us as if we were bound in traps.
Upon the vault of heaven, as the beautiful-winged one flew, those longing in their hearts gazed upon you. The golden-winged bird, messenger of Varuṇa, the restless bird in the womb of Yama.
The first-born brahman from the east — the seeker revealed the shining one beyond the boundary. He, the highest, pervades all the foundations of this one; he opened the womb of both the existent and the nonexistent.
For him who is without precedent, the most manifold — for this great hero, the mighty, the swift — for the powerful one, the thunderbolt-bearer, the most beneficent, they have fashioned these words for him, the firm one.
Indra by his power drove away the one who was blowing — he, the man-minded one, blew away the sticky hindrance.
Frightened by Vṛtra's hissing, all the gods who were your companions abandoned you. Let friendship between you and the Maruts exist, O Indra — and thus you shall conquer all these armies.
The gray-haired one swallowed the vigorous youth who was trembling in the assembly of many. Behold the power of the divine sage — he died today who was alive yesterday in the same assembly.
You, O Indra, being born among the seven, became an enemy to those who had no enemy. You found heaven and earth in their hidden place and waged war with the wide-extended worlds.
Like a pillar — you, the thunderbolt-bearer, the sharp one, the manifoldly renowned, the bull, firm in nourishment — you make your enemies yield, O Indra who desires to serve; I sing of the brilliant Vṛtra-slayer.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Bring forth praise to the great one, the greatly increasing, the far-sighted one; render good thought. Go forward through the many peoples, O you who fills all living beings.
We would invoke for good fortune the bountiful Indra, the most manly in this battle, in the winning of prizes — the mighty one who listens, for our aid in conflicts, smiting the Vṛtras, winning wealth together.
Rise up, send forth the brahman prayers seeking glory; magnify Indra in the battle, O Vasiṣṭha. He who has stretched forth all things with his fame — may he hear my words as they approach.
The wheel set in the waters — let that sweet thing please him. The udder that is stretched upon the earth — the milk he placed in the cows and in the plants.
We invoke here for our well-being Tārkṣya, the swift one who goes into battle, whose wheel-rim is unharmed.
Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the easy-to-invoke warrior Indra in every invocation — I now invoke the mighty Indra, the much-invoked. May Indra the bountiful one take this oblation.
We worship Indra with the thunderbolt in his right hand, the charioteer of the bay steeds of many ways. He who shakes his beard upward and onward, becoming terrible with his armies, advancing with his bounties.
The all-smiting, the bold, the loud-voiced Indra, the great, the boundless, the bull, bearer of the fine thunderbolt — the slayer of Vṛtra who wins the prize, the bountiful Maghavan who gives riches, the excellent bestower.
Whatever mortal assails us wishing to harm us, whether thinking himself fierce or swift — destroy him in battle, or with your strength, O Indra; may we overcome him, protected by your heroic might.
He whom the peoples striving against Vṛtras invoke, whom those rushing in the yokings invoke, whom they invoke in the winning of heroes, whom the inspired ones urge on in the contest at the water's proximity — he is Indra.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Indra and Parvata, bring here with your great chariot good nourishment, O you of good heroes. Enjoy the oblations at the sacrifice, O gods; grow great, gladdened with songs and praises.
For Indra, the songs unleashed like darting streams sent forth the waters from the bottom of the ocean. He who, like an axle by his powers, has everywhere propped up the earth and heaven.
Friends have turned you with friendship; you have gone across many floods indeed. The wise one should take hold of the father's grandson; shining more brightly in this dwelling.
Who today yokes the cattle of cosmic order to the yoke — the laboring, angry, ill-willed ones? The water-bearing one who brings welfare is near to them; he alone who paid the debt of their nurture shall live.
The singers of the Gāyatrī sing of you; those who chant the Arka-hymns adore you. The Brahmin priests, O you of a hundred powers, have stretched you upward like a bamboo pole.
All hymns have magnified Indra, ocean-wide in his expanse — the most chariot-worthy of charioteers, the true lord and master of prizes.
Drink this, Indra — the pressed soma, the foremost, the immortal exhilaration. The bright streams of sacred order pour toward you in the seat of Rita.
What gift of wonders, O wielder of the stone-bolt, is not yet given by you here? Knowing our bounty, O wealthy one, bring it with both hands.
Hear the call from afar, O Indra, of him who worships you. Fill him with wealth of good heroes and of cattle — you are truly great.
The soma has been pressed for you, O mightiest Indra — come boldly! May the sovereign power fill you, as the sun fills the sky with its rays.
Come, O Indra, with your bay steeds, to the excellent praise of Kaṇva. Directed from yonder heaven, travel through the sky, O guardian of the day.
Hymns have approached you like charioteers at the soma-pressings, O lover of song. They have lowed all around you as cows low about their calf.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Come now, let us praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure Sāman. May he, grown mighty with pure recitations, delight and be satisfied with pure blessings.
He who is richest in wealth among you, most glorious in brilliance — the pressed soma, O Indra, is your exhilaration, O lord of self-power.
Men have come to the one prepared and ready, to the one who travels on a pathless way.
Bring to us the great one who rests among the birds, the great one who dwells in the cavern, the first and foremost. You have smitten away fierce speech.
We turn your chariot as for help and for grace. O mightiest one, O true lord — Indra, the greatly active, the vanquisher of enemies.
He, the primal one, the longing of the great ones, has reached forth through his powers. Through whose doors Manu, the father, has reached forth his thoughts among the gods.
When the swift ones, resplendent, are harnessed in the chariots — drinking the intoxicating sweetness — there they win renown.
That one I praise for you, the unassailable, the lord of might — Indra, the overcomer of all, the hero most powerful in deeds, the all-knowing.
I have spoken in praise of Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the horse of might. May he make our mouths fragrant; may he extend our life-spans.
The breaker of strongholds was born young, a seer of unlimited might. Indra, the upholder of all action, the wielder of the thunderbolt, praised by many.
He seeks to win you by thought and by the rich fullness of mind, for the sake of the sacrifice.
The two who are called the yoked pair of Kaśyapa, the heaven-finders — whose universal ordinance and sacrifice the wise, having considered, observe.
Sing, sing forth, O men; sing, O you of dear wisdom. Let the young sons also sing; boldly sing the stronghold that shines.
The recitation to be proclaimed for Indra, that which increases, for the ever-besought one — so that the mighty one may rejoice among us at the soma-pressings and in companionship.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The lord of all men, the lord of the unyielding might — by these same paths, I call on the aid of the peoples and of the chariots.
He indeed who, O divine men, calms the mortal by thought — with such aid he crosses not the great heaven's enmity nor adversity.
Your bounty, O Indra, is all-pervading; your gift is wide-reaching, O you of a hundred powers. So now, O one visible to all peoples, O good giver, bestow on us brilliance.
The birds that are of your mind, the flying ones, two-footed and four-footed in the bright space — at dawn they have sprung forward following the seasons, from the ends of heaven.
You gods who stand in the middle of the luminous realm of heaven — what is the sacred order for you? What is the immortal? What is your ancient oblation?
We worship the Ṛc and the Sāman, by means of which the ritual works are performed. The two that reign in their seat shall carry the sacrifice to the gods.
In wisdom, in choice, in firm standing, in the liberal, the most fiercely mighty, the swift, the courageous.
I place trust in his primary wrath, which smote the Dasyu and opened the manly waters. Both worlds ran after you; even the earth shrinks, O stone-bolt bearer, from your fury.
Come together, all, to the lord of heaven in his might — he alone who has been the abundant host of peoples. He, the primal one, desiring to conquer the new, has turned the paths about him — he alone.
We are yours, O Indra, O much-praised, we who move about relying on you, O most abundant wealthy one. For no other than you, O lover of song, can hold our hymns together — like the earth, accept our speech toward that.
The great hymns, the mighty chants, have bellowed toward Indra, the magnanimous, the sustainer of the peoples, the invocation-worthy — grown great with pure praises, called by many, immortal, aging day by day.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Toward Indra, all thoughts — heaven-seeking, unanimous, eager — have bellowed. They have embraced him all around as women embrace a husband, like a young hero, the magnanimous one, for aid.
With your hymns exhilarate that ram, Indra the much-invoked, the hymn-worthy, the ocean of riches. The heavens do not wander beyond his human understanding; sing to him, the most bountiful, the sage.
Magnify well that ram, the heaven-finder, with whose hundred of good beings they move together. Like a swift horse toward the prize, toward the chariot that heeds the call — may we turn Indra to our aid with pure praises.
Full of ghee, of all worlds the splendor, wide and broad, the two honey-yielding, beautifully formed ones — Heaven and Earth, propped apart by the law of Varuṇa, ageless and rich in seed.
When, O Indra, you filled both worlds as the dawns fill them — you, the great one, the sovereign king of the great ones and of peoples. The divine mother gave birth to him; the auspicious mother gave birth.
Recite the word rich in nourishment to the joyful one, who with his companion drove out the black-wombed one. Desiring aid, we call the bull, thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by Maruts, for fellowship.
The growing, skilled one is known — for he is truly great.
Sing forth toward him, the much-invoked, the much-praised. Seek to win mighty Indra with your hymns.
We sing of that your exhilaration, the bull, the conqueror in battles — and the world-maker, O stone-bolt bearer, glorious with bay steeds.
When, O Indra, you rejoice in the soma with Viṣṇu, or indeed with Trita Āptya, or when you delight among the Maruts together with the soma-drops.
Pour out more of the intoxicating sweetness from the plant-juice, O Adhvaryu. For thus the hero is praised — he who is ever-growing.
Pour the soma-drop for Indra — he drinks the soma sweetness. He urges on bounties with his greatness.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Come now, friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns — he alone who surpasses all peoples.
Sing the Sāman to Indra, the great to the great inspired one — to the maker of prayer, the wise, the praiseworthy.
He who alone knows how to bestow wealth on the mortal who gives — the ruling, unimpeded Indra, verily.
Friends, let us learn the prayer for Indra the thunderbolt-bearer. I shall praise well the most heroic, the bold one among you.
I praise that might of yours, O Indra, supreme among the divine — that by which you, O lord of power, smash Vṛtra with your strength.
In whose exhilaration you subdued that Śambara for Divodāsa — this is that Soma, O Indra, pressed out for you; drink.
Come to us, O Indra, dear one, unconquerable winner of all, broad on every side like a mountain, lord of the sky.
That rapture of yours, O Indra, mightiest Soma-drinker, which wakens within you — by which you strike down the devourer — that we implore.
For nourishment and vigor, grant us therefore a longer life to live. O Ādityas of equal power, make it so.
For you, O thunderbolt-handed one, know how to ward off the snares of destruction, day by day, as the purifier wards off the encircling dangers.
Drive away disease, drive away the oppressor of the household, drive away ill will. O Ādityas, keep distress far from us.
Drink the Soma, O Indra; let it gladden you — the Soma that the stone has well-pressed for you, O driver of bay horses, well-drawn from the presser's arms like a swift steed.
Even in battle you seek fellowship.
Him who in former times brought us this and this abundance — him I now praise before you, O friends, Indra, for his protection.
Come, do not be harmed, you who are ready to depart; do not fall back, you of equal zeal — you who strive to hold even what is firm.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Come here for the Soma-drop, O lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fertile fields. Drink the Soma, O lord of Soma.
With you truly as ally, O bull, we would challenge the snorting foe in the gathering of the cattle-rich folk.
Even the cows of equal zeal, the Maruts bound by common kinship, lick the peaks in turns.
Bring us, O Indra, strength and manly power, O lord of a hundred plans, all-seeing one — a hero who can withstand battles.
And so, O Indra, lover of hymns, we approach you in desire, we rush toward you — like waters rising upward to the heights.
They settle in you as birds settle in a cow-enriched, sweet, intoxicating, spreading place. We bow before you again and again, O Indra.
We, too, O incomparable one, carrying you like some great unsupported load, desiring help, call upon you, O brilliant thunderbolt-bearer.
Those who together with Indra, the bull, exult in joy, the splendid ones rich in treasure — following him in his own sovereign rule.
For thus indeed this Soma-intoxication made the sacred word a source of increase. O mightiest thunderbolt-bearer, you cut the serpent out of the earth by your strength, singing praise — following your own sovereign rule.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has grown great with exhilaration and strength, with his heroes. We invoke his aid in great combats and in small — may he drive us forward to victories.
For you alone, O Indra, O stone-wielder, O thunderbolt-bearer, is that valor unconquerable. Indeed with that your magic you slew that magic beast — singing praise, following your own sovereign rule.
Go forward, rush on, be bold — your thunderbolt shall not be laid down. O Indra, for manly power is your strength; slay Vṛtra, win the waters — singing praise, following your own sovereign rule.
When the battles break forth, wealth is bestowed on the bold one. Yoke your two bay steeds, shaken by rapture — whom will you strike? Whom will you place in wealth? Place us, O Indra, in wealth.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
They have eaten their fill, they have been gladdened; the beloved ones have bent down. The self-luminous poets have praised with the newest thought. Now yoke your two bay steeds, O Indra.
Listen closely to these words, O bountiful one, as to a mother's. When will you render us, who possess true speech, to our purpose here? Now yoke your two bay steeds, O Indra.
The moon within the waters, the fair-winged one runs through the sky. The lightnings with golden rims do not find your footprint. Know this, O heaven and earth, on my behalf.
The praiser adorns with his hymns your most beloved chariot, O Aśvins — the bull-like one, wealth-carrying. Hear my sweet invocation in return.
That praiseworthy blazing one of yours glows in battle. Bring forth quickly for the praisers.
Like Agni, with our own hymns we choose you as the invoking priest — swift, of purifying flame. In your exhilaration you speak out in the sacrifices where the ritual grass is spread.
Awaken us today, O Uṣas, for great wealth, O celestial one. Just as you have awakened us, O one of true renown, O airy one, O well-born one, O dawn with horses and truth.
Blow into us a blessed mind, discernment, and resolve. Then in your friendship, in the exhilaration of the Soma drink, you speak out — the cows rejoice as if at pasture.
By his might the great, terrible strength returns again and again in due course. The handsome one, with his helmet, set the iron thunderbolt in the hands of the two glorious ones nearby.
He indeed mounts that bull-like chariot that wins cattle — he who perceives the full bowl yoked with bay steeds. Now yoke your two bay steeds, O Indra.
I regard as Agni the one who is a treasure-home, to whom the milch-cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, the constant prize-winners. Bring nourishment quickly for the praisers.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
No distress, no evil reaches that mortal, O gods, whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa, with one accord, lead beyond hatred.
Run forth all around for the winning of prizes, overcoming obstacles on every side. You go to overcome enemies, as if to discharge a debt.
Flow, O Soma, great as the ocean, the father of gods, encompassing all dwellings.
Flow, O Soma, for great discernment — like a horse rubbed clean, a prize-winner for wealth.
The lovely drop has entered the filter, for exhilaration — the seer in the lap of the waters, for good fortune.
For we rejoice in you, O pressed Soma, in the great sovereign rule of battle. You, O Pavamāna, plunge forward toward the prizes.
Who are these manifest men, nest-mates, the youths of Rudra — then those with good horses?
O Agni, today with hymns, like a horse, may we succeed in that blessed resolve that touches the heart — may we thrive through your urgings.
The youths have come forth, the prize-winning ones have come toward the prize at the impulsion of god Savitṛ. Win the heavenly track, O steeds.
Flow, O Soma, full of brilliance, of fine streams, great, unobstructed, in due order.
O all-giving one, bring to us from all sides — you whom we implore as most mighty.
This is the sacred priest who is in season — I praise the one famed as Indra by name.
The priests, magnifying Indra with hymns, strengthened him for the slaying of the serpent.
They fashioned the chariot for the horse; Tvaṣṭā forged the brilliant thunderbolt for the much-invoked one.
Auspicious is the step, the bounty, the desire of the wealthy man; the one who lacks vows neither impels nor touches riches.
Ever pure are the cows, nourishing all things; ever blameless are the gods.
Come with the forest; the cows with their udders follow the path.
Dwelling beside the honey-sweet refreshment, may we thrive in wealth; we hold meditation on you, O Indra.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The Maruts sing the hymn of praise; the youthful, renowned Indra responds with his shout of glory.
Sing forth to Indra, the foremost slayer of Vṛtra, the inspired sage — sing the song that he delights in.
O Agni, you are our nearest kin and our protector; be auspicious, be our shelter.
Agni, brilliant like Bhaga, bestows the gem upon those of great might.
Shout forth before all things; whether it was won of old or is won here now.
Dawn, most beneficent of sisters, rolls the path along by her noble birth.
May we prosper these worlds — both Indra and all the gods together.
As rivers spread along their courses, O Indra, so may your gifts flow forth.
By this may we win the prize established by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in brave sons.
Mitra and Varuṇa make the refreshing draughts swell with strength; make our nourishment rich, O Indra.
Indra reigns over all things.
He rejoiced to perform the great deed; the great, vast one — the god accompanied the god, the true Soma the true Indra.
This one, the thought of the seers, is visible to a thousand men, a light that upholds the law; the mighty one set the Dawns in alignment — the blameless, like-minded ones, ardent in their day, discerning of the cow.
Come to us, O Indra, from afar, onward toward us as a true lord of the assembly, as a king who is a true lord. We invoke you, offering forth at the pressings, as sons invoke a father, the most bountiful one, for the winning of the prize.
I loudly call on that Indra, the bountiful, the mighty, who holds undivided and unchallenged fame in abundance; most generous, he has turned back with our hymns, the worshipful one; may the wielder of the thunderbolt make all good paths open to us for wealth.
Let there be a call to hear; set Agni forward with thought; now we choose that divine host, we choose Indra and Vāyu. When the active ones bind at the navel for Vivasvat renewed, then now the prayers go forth toward the gods, as prayers indeed.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Let your great praises go forth to Viṣṇu accompanied by the Maruts, born of the mountain — Evayāmarut. Forward to the host, to the worshipful one, to the joyous one, to the powerful, to the glorious purpose, to the one of roaring vows, for strength.
Purifying himself with this golden radiance, he crosses all hatreds along with his yokemates, like the sun with his yokemates. The stream of his back shines as the tawny, ruddy one purifies himself. As he passes through all forms with the Ṛk verses, with the seven-mouthed Ṛk verses.
I hymn that god Savitṛ, of bold resolve, with both my hands — the true impeller, dwelling in gems — with the dear thought; he whose thought blazed upward in radiance at the impulse; golden-handed, of bright resolve, he measured out the sky with grace.
I honor Agni the Hotṛ, generous, son of strength, the all-knowing, inspired like the all-knowing one; who, upright and well-sacrificing, a god by divine grace, follows the blazing of ghee, the bright-flaming one, as the clarified butter is poured.
That heroic deed of yours, O manly Indra, was done first of all in heaven, worthy to be proclaimed; you who by the god's strength set the rivers flowing as you caused the waters to flow. You have become all things beyond the gods in power; the hundred-crafted one has found strength, has found refreshment.
What is born of your invigorating draught, high in heaven, dwelling on the earth — mighty shelter, great renown.
Flow with your sweetest, most exhilarating stream, O Soma; pressed, you flow for Indra to drink.
Flow forth as a bull with your stream, and exhilarating for him who has the Maruts, bearing all things with your might.
With that exhilaration of yours which is most choice, flow forth with your juice — slayer of the demon, defender of the divine hero.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Three voices rise up; the cows low, the milch cows cry; the tawny one comes lowing aloud.
Purify yourself, O drop, for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, most rich in sweetness; sit down in the womb of the hymn.
The shoot has been pressed for exhilaration; the dexterous one stands on the mountains in the waters; like a falcon he has sat down in his birthplace.
Purify yourself, accomplishing power, O tawny one, for the gods to drink — exhilaration for the Maruts, for Vāyu.
The roaring one standing on the mountains, Soma has flowed around the filter; in exhilarations you are the bearer of all things.
The seer, dear to heaven, placed among the grandchildren's birds, goes forth with his sounds, the one of bold resolve.
The pressed drops have stepped forward at the sacred assembly.
The wise Soma juices flow forth, the waves lead the waters, like great buffaloes through the forests.
Purify yourself, O drop, a bull when pressed; make us glorious among the people; smite away all enemies.
For you are truly a bull by your radiance; we invoke you, the brilliant one, O self-purifying one, who sees the heavenly light.
The drop has entered the filter, the conscious one, dear as the thought of the seers; he releases the horse as a charioteer.
The vigorous Soma juices have been released forward, seeking cattle, seeking horses; the bright, swift ones seeking heroes.
Purify yourself, O god, extending life; let your exhilaration go to Indra; mount Vāyu by the law.
The self-purifying one has begotten the brilliant light of heaven, like thunder; the great light belonging to all men.
The drops, the Indu juices, flow around for exhilaration with powerful song; they rush with their stream of sweetness.
The seer has flowed around and settled on the wave of the river; bearing the singer, much-desired.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Come near to the one just born, swift-moving, purified with the cows' milk; the gods have eagerly approached the drop of Soma.
Purifying himself, the all-seeing one strides forth against all enemies; they adorn the inspired sage with their thoughts.
Entering the vessel as he is pressed, streaming forth toward all glories, the drop of Soma is poured out for Indra.
Like a chariot-horse he has been released; pressed out, he flows through the filter in the two bowls; the steed has strode along the course.
When, like rushing cows, the swift streams strode forth, striking off the dark skin.
Driving away enemies as you purify yourself, O Soma, knower of sacred rites, exhilarating one — push away the ungodly people.
Purify yourself with that stream by which you caused the sun to shine, impelling the waters destined for mankind.
Purify yourself, you who have aided Indra to smite Vṛtra — him who had enveloped the great waters.
Flow around with this offering, O drop, you who in your raptures have driven away the ninety and nine.
Flow, roaring one, through the filter to Bharadvāja — the heaven-dwelling, ever-victorious one — with the Soma draught.
He flashes together with the sun.
Today we choose your healing and bliss-bringing power, the carrier much-longed-for, the protector.
O Adhvaryu, bring the Soma pressed with the stones to the filter; purify it for Indra to drink.
That gladdening stream of the pressed Soma flows crossing over; that gladdening one flows crossing over.
Purify yourself, O Soma, flowing toward wealth of a thousandfold, full of heroic might; pour upon us your glories.
The ancient human sages stepped on the newer path; they generated the sun for its splendor.
Flow, O Soma, most brilliant, roaring toward the wooden troughs; settle in your proper stations, in the womb places.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You are a bull, O Soma, luminous; a bull, O god, with a bull's vow; as a bull you have upheld the laws.
Purify yourself with your stream for refreshment, being cleansed by the wise; O drop, go toward the cows with your radiance.
O Soma, purify yourself with your exhilarating stream, O bull, seeking the gods, through the wool-filters, longing for us.
By this, O Soma, protecting good deeds and being great, you have increased yourself; being impelled you indeed pour forth as a bull.
This all-seeing one is placed in motion; the Pavamāna is alive and aware; being spurred on, he impels the vast watery realm.
Flow forth for us, O drop, not bearing a great wave against us; you hasten toward the gods.
Soma drives away the enemies, he flows, washing away the churlish; going to his proper place in Indra.
O bestower of treasures, take your seat in the womb of the truth; O golden divine spring, flow forth.
Pour around the pressed Soma, he who is the highest offering; the manly one who has run swiftly, who has pressed Soma with the stones in the midst of the waters.
O Soma, roaring, pressed with stones, pass through the wool filters of the sheep; like a man entering a stronghold, the tawny one enters the two bowls and takes his seat in the forests.
Flow forth, O Soma, for the delight of the gods, swelling with flood like a river; the invigorating, wakeful juice of the Soma plant streams toward the honey-dripping vessel.
Soma, being pressed by the pressers upon the pressing stones from the sheep's wool, goes with a tawny stream like two horses; he goes with an exhilarating stream.
O Soma, I rejoice in your friendship, O drop, day by day; many things, O tawny one, move against me — protect me from them, going around that boundary, come.
Being cleansed by the skilled hands, you set speech in motion in the sea; purifying yourself, you flow forward with tawny, abundant, much-desired wealth.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The human Soma-drops purify themselves, an intoxicating joy; upon the ridge of the ocean, the wise and exhilarating ones, dropping with rapture.
O Soma, purifying yourself, ever wakeful, beloved as you flow around through the wool filters; you have become the inspired sage, the most like Aṅgiras — sprinkle our sacrifice with honey.
The rapturous Soma, pressed for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, flows with a thousandfold stream past the wool filter; men cleanse him.
Purify yourself, O most powerful winner of prizes, flowing toward all desirable things; you are the ocean, O Soma, exhilarating one, the first to spread the laws for the gods.
The purifying ones have been released, flowing over the filter with their stream; accompanied by the Maruts, exhilarating, belonging to Indra, they hasten toward the sacrifice, toward the oblations and toward wisdom.
Cleansing you like a prize-winning horse, they lead you with reins toward the sacred grass.
Speaking forth poetic wisdom like Uśanas, the divine one proclaims the origins of the gods; great in vow, pure in alliance, the purifier, the boar comes forward on foot, roaring.
The carrier stirs three utterances, the thought of truth, the wisdom of sacred prayer; the cows go seeking the lord of cows, the inspired thoughts go, longing, toward Soma.
Impelled by his impulse and drive, being purified, this god has mingled his essence with the gods; pressed and roaring, he goes around the filter like a friend, a hotar with cattle, going about his dwelling.
Soma purifies himself, the begetter of inspired thoughts, the begetter of heaven, the begetter of earth; the begetter of fire, the begetter of the sun, the begetter of Indra, and the begetter of Viṣṇu.
The voices have called out to the three-ridged, bull-like bestower of sustenance, the resounding one; clothed in the forest plants, like Varuṇa among rivers, the bestower of treasures distributes desirable things.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The ocean has strode first over the spreading ordinance, generating progeny, the guardian of the world; the bull upon the ridge, on the sheep's filter, the great Soma has grown, roaring like a pressing stone.
The tawny one, roaring as he is poured out, settling purified in the belly of the wood; directed by men, he strips the hide from the cow, and from there, with his natural powers, he generates inspired thought.
This is the honey-sweet Soma of yours, O Indra, the bull belonging to the bull — he has flowed around the filter; the giver of thousands, the giver of hundreds, the great giver, has repeatedly taken his stand at the sacred grass as the prize-winner.
Purify yourself, O Soma, honey-sweet, rich in truth, clothed in the waters upon the woolly ridge; descend into the ghee-filled troughs, most inebriating, exhilarating, drunk by Indra.
Making good things for his friends who call upon Indra, Soma puts on his impetuous garments.
Your honey-sweet streams have been released, having passed through the barrier when purified, past the wool; O Pavamāna, you purify yourself as you generate the station of the cows, and you have swelled the sun with your rays.
Sing forth, let us praise the gods; urge Soma on for great riches; may the sweet one purify himself past the woolen filter, may the divine drop take his seat in the vessel.
Pressing forward, the begetter of heaven and earth, like a chariot, has gone forward to win the prize; going to Indra, sharpening his weapons, he has placed all good things in his hands.
When the speech of the mind's beloved, foremost in excellence, fashions the law on the shining front, then the eager cows, longing, come along to the bowl, to Soma their beloved lord.
Together the ten sisters, the thoughts of the wise one, cleanse the bull as they flow onward. The golden one ran around, the offspring of the Sun; like a swift steed he entered the trough.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
When upon him, gleaming like a prize-winning mare, the inspired thoughts contend as peoples around the sun, he flows choosing the waters, seeking wisdom, for a thought that enlarges the herd like an enclosure.
The swift Indu flows, the flood that yields the cow; Soma exhilarates Indra together for rapture. He slays the demon, drives away all hostility, creating wide space — he is the king of the stronghold.
With this purifying stream, flow, bringing these treasures; Indra has drunk deeply and sped to the lake. Even the tawny one, whose impulse is like the wind, the much-wise one places a man for the discerning.
Great is what Soma the mighty buffalo did when, the embryo of the waters, he chose the gods. The purifying Indu placed might in Indra; he begot light in the Sun.
He was released, the eloquent one, like a chariot-horse in battle — the foremost wisdom shaped by thought and mind. The ten sisters on the back of the sheep cleanse the carrier toward the seats.
Like the surging waves of the waters rushing forward, the inspired thoughts set Soma in motion. Reverently they approach him, come together and enter — the longing ones entering him who longs.
As forerunners for your pressed drink, the inebriating Soma, O friends, pierce and drive away the long-tongued dog.
This Soma, Pūṣan, wealth, and Bhaga, flows along purifying himself. Lord of all existence, he looks out upon both worlds.
The pressed Somas, most full of sweetness, gladdening for Indra, flow purified through the filter. May your ecstasies go to the gods.
The Somas, the drops, flow purified for us, most knowing of the path. Friendly, well-pressed, unblemished, sweetly meditating, finding the sun.
Flow toward us the most prize-winning wealth, coveted by hundreds, O Indu — of a thousand forms, of mighty splendor, overpowering with brilliance.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
They celebrate the beloved, the desired of Indra, who does no harm. As mothers lick a newborn calf in its first life, so they tend him.
For the beloved bold one they stretch out manhood like a bow. The bright ones go forth for the mighty lord's gleaming robe, the great ones honoring the sage foremost.
They purify with the fleece that beloved, tawny, brown Soma, who goes around all the gods together with his rapture.
Of the one being pressed, of his drink, no mortal craves that speech. Drive away the ungrateful dog; smite the arrogant one as the Bhṛgus did.
Upon the great chariot of the great Sun, the all-seeing one mounted, spreading in all directions.
May the drops, the Indus, urged onward press forward for us; the tawny ones, well-pressed, lofty among the gods. Let the eager energies conquer even the hostile ones; may they be friendly to us and win our inspired thoughts.
This sweet one roars forward in the bowl, Indra's thunderbolt, most wondrous of wonders. The good milch-cows, dripping with ghee, flowing for him who is approaching, roar and rush with their milk.
Indu has gone forth to Indra's appointed place; as a friend to a friend he does not diminish their shared speech. Like a young man with maidens, Soma flows together in the bowl by the hundredfold-traveled path.
The supporter of heaven flows, the active essence, the power to be celebrated by men among the gods. Released, the tawny one like a swift horse among heroes freely makes his displays in the rivers.
The all-seeing bull of inspired thoughts, Soma, flows purified — the extender of days, of dawns, of heaven. He has roared into the bowls, the breath of the rivers, entering into Indra's heart with the wise ones.
Three times the seven cows milked for him the true mixture in the highest heaven. Four other worlds he fashioned for his gleaming robe when he grew great with the rites.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Soma, well-pressed, flow all around for Indra; let disease be gone, together with the demon. May the deceitful ones not enjoy your essence; let the drops be here for the wealthy devotees.
Soma the ruddy bull, the tawny pair, has been pressed; like a skillful king he has roared toward the cows. Purifying himself, he will pass through the eternal fleece; like a falcon he has sat in the ghee-rich womb.
The sweet drops have flowed toward the god, they have flowed like milch-cows to a gathering. Seated on the sacred grass, the divine cows with their udders, they assumed the garment of the flowing dawn-cow.
They anoint, they anoint distinctly, they anoint together; they lick the will; they anoint with richness. Those with golden purifiers seize the bull flying in the swelling breath of the river, the animal in the waters.
Your filter is spread out, O Lord of Prayer; mighty, you encompass the limbs from all sides. One whose body has not been heated, the raw one, does not attain that — only the well-cooked who carry it fully reach that.
Born to be heard, the drops, the Indus, are finders of the sun.
Speed forward, O Soma, wakeful; O Indu, flow all around for Indra. Bring the brilliant vital force, the finder of the sun.
Friends, sit down; sing forth for the purifying one. Adorn him like a child with sacrificial rites for splendor.
Friends, sing toward him, the purifying one, for your rapture. Sweetening him like a child with oblations and with praises.
The child of the great ones breathes, urging forward the shining thought of Order. He became beloved of all, then twofold.
Flow pure for the pleasure of the gods, O Indu, with your streams of might. Fill the bowl, O sweet Soma, our seat.
