Soma, purifying himself with his wave, courses through the woolen filter. The purifying one, roaring aloud, goes at the forefront of speech.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Speech is uttered forth for the purifying, wise Soma. Like one bringing a burden, he delights with inspired thoughts.
Like one rich in cattle and horses, O Indu, pressed forth, O skillful one, like a bowman — sustain your pure bright hue among the cows.
The voices have sounded toward you for us, the finder of wealth. We clothe your bright hue with the cows' streams.
The beloved tawny one flows, moving swiftly past the crooked places with speed. Flow toward the praisers, glory rich in heroes.
Soma flows purifying himself around the honey-dripping bowl. The seven voices of the seers have sounded toward him.
Great is the most heavenly rapture.
Shine forth, O lord of impulses, of great fame and splendor, O god, god-seeking. Split open the middle bowl, O young one.
Let the pressers pour around, like a swift horse, the praise that is nimble, crossing the atmosphere, dripping through the wood, swelling with the waters.
This one, who causes rapture to flow, with a thousand streams, the bull that milks heaven, bearing all good things.
He is pressed who is the bringer of riches, of wealth, of refreshments — the Soma who belongs to those who dwell well.
For you indeed, O purifying one, are the most brilliant of divine births, proclaiming for the sake of immortality.
This one, pressed forth, flows most intoxicating with the streams, through the woolen filters, playing like a wave of the waters.
He who with his might cut free the dawn-cows and those hidden within the rock. You have stretched toward the enclosure rich in cattle and horses — break it boldly like armor. Oṃ — break it boldly like armor.
O Indra, bring to us the foremost, most powerful glory. When we would hold firm both heaven and earth, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O fair-cheeked one, you have filled them both.
Indra is king of the world, of all peoples — whatever of all forms is his pervades the earth. From that wealth he gives to the worshipper; he who urges on, though praised, comes forward.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
His is this realm — yoked for the contest, for the people, the forest, the sun: great is the delight of Indra.
Loosen from us the highest snare, O Varuṇa, and loose the lowest; unloose the middle one. Then, O Āditya, in your covenant may we be sinless, free for Aditi.
Through you, O Soma flowing bright, may we gather perpetually the treasure won in battle. May Mitra and Varuṇa magnify that for us, and Aditi, the River, the Earth, and Heaven.
Make this one bull — make me this alone.
Flow around and grant wide space for us — for Indra the worshipful, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts.
With this may we, desiring to win, obtain all the glories of humankind, O lord.
I am the firstborn of the cosmic order; I bear the name of immortality before the gods. Whoever gives to me — thus does he declare — I, being food, eat him who eats no food.
In the Paruṣṇī rivers flows the bright milk.
The dappled one, the dawn, blazed forth; the bull, foremost among cows, bellows seeking strength throughout the worlds. Wise seers measured out his magic with his magic; the fathers, beholding men, received the embryo.
Indra alone — together with his two bay horses, yoked by his word — is mixed in with them. Indra, the thunderbolt-wielder, is golden.
O Indra, protect us in contests and in the thousand-prize races, O mighty one, with your mighty aids.
He whose name is Pratha and Sapratha — the offering of the Anuṣṭubh hymn, which is an oblation — from Dhātar shining bright and from Savitṛ and Viṣṇu, Vasiṣṭha brought forth the Rathantara chant.
Come, O Vāyu, with your team of horses; this bright one is offered to you. You shall go to the home of the one who presses the soma.
When you were born, O bountiful one, peerless, for the slaying of Vṛtra — then you spread out the earth, and you propped up the sky.
May Parameṣṭhin Prajāpati make firm in heaven as he makes firm the sky.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
May your milky streams come together, may your strengths come together, may your virile powers come together, O soma that overwhelms the foe. Waxing to fullness for immortality, O Soma, place your highest glories in the sky.
You, O Soma, are all these plants; you gave birth to the waters; you produced the cows. You stretched out the wide mid-air; you with your light drove away the darkness.
I praise Agni, the household priest, the divine minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, the greatest bestower of treasure.
They conceived the first name of the cows; thrice seven the highest name they knew among peoples. Knowing those names, the dawning ones sang out — the ruddy, glorious cows appeared upon the earth.
Some go together, others come flowing together; the rivers fill the same trough. The pure waters flow toward him — pure, shining bright, the child of waters who does not eat food.
The auspicious young maiden of day has come forward, stirring up the banners of light. Night has become the auspicious one who brings to rest all the moving world.
Now of the mighty, ruddy, vigorous one declare to the assembly our speech for Jātavedas. A fresh pure thought flows clear as soma for the dear Agni Vaiśvānara.
Let all the gods hear my sacrifice — both heaven and earth, and the child of the waters — hear my hymn. May I not speak words reprehensible to you; in your graces may we rejoice to the utmost.
May heaven and earth grant me glory; may Indra and Bṛhaspati grant me glory. May Bhaga's glory find me; may glory be released toward me. May I be a proclaimer of glory at this seat of the glorious one.
Now I will proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, the first great acts that the thunderbolt-wielder performed. He slew the serpent; he bored through the flank; he split open the bellies of the mountains.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
I am Agni by birth, Jātavedas by name; clarified butter is my eye, immortality my mouth. The hymn of three elements, the measurer of the atmosphere — I am the ceaseless light, I am all the oblation.
Agni guards the foremost step of the bird; the swift one guards the track of the sun. Agni guards at the navel of the seven-headed one.
O Agni, you who find wealth — with milk you have granted us radiance to behold.
Spring is indeed delightful; summer is indeed delightful. After the rains come autumn; winter is indeed delightful; cool season is indeed delightful.
The Cosmic Person has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. Encompassing the earth on all sides, he extends beyond it by ten fingers.
Three-quarters of the Cosmic Person rose upward; one quarter of him was born again here. Thence he strode out in all directions over what eats and what does not eat.
The Cosmic Person alone is all this — whatever has been and whatever shall be. He is the lord of immortality, and also of whatever grows beyond by food. All beings constitute one quarter of him; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.
Such is his greatness, yet greater still is the Cosmic Person. He is the lord of immortality, and of all that grows and flourishes through food.
From him Virāj was born; from Virāj the Cosmic Person arose. Being born, he surpassed the earth from behind and also from in front.
I hold you two, O Heaven and Earth, as those of good nourishment, you who have spread out immeasurably and boundlessly. O Heaven and Earth, be gracious to us and release us from distress.
Your beard, O Indra, is tawny gold, and your two bay steeds are golden. You are praised by the poets, the sages who dwell in the woods.
Whatever brilliance gold possesses, whatever brilliance the cows possess, and the brilliance of truth and sacred prayer — with that let us be endowed.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
He gave us strength together, O Indra; for he is master of this great power, O mighty one. Like wisdom, like manly valor and steadfast strength — make us smite our enemies among the foes.
Rise up together with your bulls, with your calves, bearing all forms, you whose udders are twofold. Let this broad wide space be yours; may these waters here be easy to drink.
Drive away misfortune from afar.
May the resplendent, mighty one drink the sweet soma-drink, bestowing long life on the lord of the sacrifice, undivided. He who is wind-impelled, who protects the people by himself, nourishes them abundantly, and shines in many ways.
The wondrous face of the gods has risen up — the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. He has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere. O Sun, you are the soul of all that moves and stands still.
This dappled bull stepped forth; he sat down before his mother. Going toward his father, he entered the realm of light.
Moving within, the luminous one breathes in and breathes out. The mighty bull has illumined heaven.
In thirty stations he shines forth; speech is offered to the bird. He responds each day with rays of light.
Like thieves those stars depart with the darkness of night, before the all-seeing Sun.
His bright rays have been seen spreading among the people, blazing like fires.
Swift, visible to all, O Sun, you are the maker of light. You illuminate the entire luminous realm.
You rise toward the hosts of gods; you rise toward mankind. You rise toward all the world to behold the light of heaven.
With that purifying eye of yours, O Varuṇa, you behold the active and bustling people.
You traverse the broad realm of space, measuring out the days with your rays. O Sun, you behold all created beings.
The Sun has yoked the seven shining mares, daughters of his chariot. By them he travels, self-harnessed.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Seven bay mares carry you in your chariot, O divine Sun. O flame-haired, far-seeing one.
Know, O Maghavan, know the path in the directions that have been proclaimed. Teach us, O lord of mighty deeds, O Purūvasu, of many ancient gifts.
With aids of conquest thou art the conqueror; the soma ray is thine own. O all-knowing one, enlighten us, O Indra, for glory and for nourishment.
For so does Śakra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, come for wealth and sustenance. O mightiest thunderbolt-bearer, thou dost adorn thyself; O most munificent thunderbolt-bearer, thou dost adorn thyself. Come, drink, and be exhilarated.
Know wealth and heroic strength; become lord of victories, following according to will. O most munificent thunderbolt-bearer, thou dost adorn thyself, thou who art the mightiest among heroes.
He who is most bountiful among the givers of gifts, his soma ray blazes like fire. The all-wise one, may Indra lead us onward; he is known — praise him.
For Śakra is the master; we call upon him for protection, the conqueror who is never vanquished. May he set us beyond our foes in the heavenly realm; great is his will, his hymn, and his cosmic order.
We call upon Indra for the winning of wealth, the conqueror who is never vanquished. May he place us in the solar realm beyond our foes; may he place us in the solar realm beyond our foes.
Of thine that is ancient, O crusher of stones, the soma draught is for exhilaration. Bestow well-being upon us, O Vasu; O mightiest one, fulfillment is proclaimed. For Śakra, the sovereign, now lays down the new body.
O lord of the people, O slayer of Vṛtra, let us declare thee in battles. The hero who goes forth among the cattle, the friend who is gracious and undeceitful.
Even so, O serpent — so indeed. Even so, O Agni. Even so, O Indra. Even so, O Pūṣan. Even so, O gods. Oṃ — even so, O gods.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Flow forth, O rain-giver; bring us the wave of the waters from heaven. May the abundant nourishments be free of disease.
Flow forth with that stream by which the cattle have come hither, and the people to our home.
Flow as clarified butter in a stream, O most desired of the gods in sacrifices. Flow down your rain for us.
Run through the purifying filter in a stream for our strength and vigor. The gods shall indeed hear him.
The purifying Soma has flowed forth, has driven away the demons, illuminating the lights of praise as in ancient times.
For him who is fit to go, who has set out on the path that never retreats, O men.
Come forth to meet him, the greatest drinker of Soma, with the Soma juices; meet Indra, who bears the Soma dregs, with the pressed drops in the vessels.
If you adorn yourselves with the pressed drops, the Soma juices, the wise one who knows all things goes boldly forth to him.
For this one and that one, O Adhvaryu, carry forth the pressed Soma as food. Whether perchance of his noble, vigorous troop, he shall sound forth against the reviler.
Drive away the dog who lacks generosity; smite the arrogant one as the Bhṛgus did. Sing a hymn to Soma.
He has clothed himself in the mantle of his kinsmen, like a son in the lap of the two parents. He who flows like a lover to the women, like a suitor taking his seat in the womb — purify with the stones released from the hand the pressed Soma. Flow, O honey-bearers, with honey.
He is the hero, the accomplisher of might, who has propped apart the two worlds. The tawny one has clothed himself in the purifying filter; like a priest he has taken his seat in the womb. Sit down with reverence; curdle it toward the curd. Set the drop in Indra.
Flow, O Soma, slayer of enemies, wide-seeing, bringing blessing to the cow, fulfilling desire for the gods.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You are poured out, O Soma, for Indra to drink, for exhilaration. He is lord of the mind, the very embodiment of mind.
O purifying Soma, bestow on us wealth with excellent heroes. O drop, unite us with Indra.
You seek fellowship even in battle; you go to the archer, O Sun.
You find no wealthy one for friendship; your horses drink eagerly. When you make the river roar and sweep it along, then you are called upon like a father, O new one. He who with the strength of his arms broke ninety-nine forts — and Vṛtrahan also slew the serpent.
May that Indra, an auspicious friend, bring us what is rich in horses, in cattle, in barley. He is milked like a wide-flowing stream.
O Indra, let your tawny, long-maned steeds yoked with prayer carry you for the drinking of Soma. He who, wind-impelled, protects the creatures of himself, sustains them manifoldly and reigns far and wide.
May the two tawny steeds with peacock tails, white-backed, draw you in the golden chariot to drink of the honey-sweet pressing, to imbibe the rousing draught. The most glorious, sublimely borne, the mightiest winner of prizes — the true law of heaven set firm in its foundation — he was born as light, the slayer of enemies, the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the slayer of Asuras, the slayer of rivals.
Drink of this, O lover of praise, of the pressed juice as one who drinks first. This pressing is adorned and savory; the lovely exhilaration rules it. This is the best and highest light among lights; it is called the great all-conquering, wealth-winning one. All-shining in splendor, the great Sun, visible far and wide, has spread broadly together with indestructible might.
O much-invoked one, instruct us in this path of him who springs up from the wood, who leaps upward. May we attain the light of life.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The bull of a thousand streams, yielding milk, dear to the divine birth. He who, born of cosmic order, has grown mightily by cosmic order — the divine king, the great cosmic order. May unknown hostile places and malevolent beings not step down upon us; may the inauspicious not tread us down. With you, O hero, we shall cross over the waters flowing downward forever.
The bright one kindled and offered — O lord of the good, protect all our singers both by day and by night.
The father of the father, flashing in the womb of the mother, in the imperishable syllable, taking his seat in the lap of cosmic order — the crusher, the hero, the generous one, mighty in gifts, mingled together for vigor. Both your arms, O hundred-powered one, the bulls that have released the thunderbolt downward.
Bring a prayer bearing offspring, O Jātavedas, wide-seeing, O Agni, that which shone in heaven.
The pressed one roaring goes around the purifying filter, like a friend to the dwelling. We call upon Sarasvan, the Hotṛ who possesses cattle.
Clothed in auspicious common garments, the great sage proclaiming utterances of praise — flow back into the two bowls as you are purified, wide-seeing, awake in the divine feast.
The beloved one is also wiped clean on the woolen filter, the most glorious, dwelling among the glorious, among us. Sound forth, flowing through the straining cloth as you are purified. Do you always protect us with blessings.
May Sarasvatī cherish him who has grown great with pure praises, who has pure blessings; may she be worthy of hymns.
O pure Indra, come to us; pure, with pure aids. Being pure, hold wealth firm; being pure, rejoice in the Soma, O Soma-drinker.
O Indra, being pure you grant us wealth; pure, you bestow jewels on the worshiper. Being pure you smite the obstacles; being pure you will win the prize.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
May he who is the guardian of divine wealth inspire our prayers.
May Agni, the priest who is among men, find pleasure in our songs; may he worship the divine folk. O Lord of prayer, make the sound of the soma-pressings resound — he who is Kakṣīvant, son of Uśij.
You, O Agni, are widely famed, the beloved, the most excellent priest. Through you they spread out the sacrifice. O Agni, as you purify, pour forth life-force, strength and refreshment for us; drive away misfortune far from us.
Clothed in forests, like Varuṇa over the rivers, the dispenser of treasures distributes desirable gifts; great indeed is his sovereign power among the gods.
O hero of the host, possessing all champions, forceful conqueror — flow pure, winner of wealth. Sharp-weaponed, swift-bowed, unassailable in battles, vanquishing foes in combats — those who rival truth with truth seize vigour and keen power; the two guileless gods grow strong.
Creating wide pastures free from fear, the two accordant ones — flow pure together in full wisdom. Seeking the waters, the dawns, and the heavenly light, roar aloud great prizes for us. The rain-heavens, lords of the flowing, gift-laden waters, seize upon the lofty chariot-seat.
You slay the obstructing foes without opposition; alone you drive back the enemy, sustaining all people — the shining lights gleam in heaven.
Now we implore you, O Asura of great wisdom, for wealth and a share of bounty. Like a great hide, your protection, O Indra — may your favours reach us. They yoke his two beloved tawny steeds, bright-winged, to the chariot, ruddy, bold, and man-bearing.
Making a signal for the signalless, a form for the formless — O manly one, you were born together with the dawns.
You of excellent will for this sacrifice — that which you have made, you have chosen; you have selected the drop, the soma for joy and for the yoke.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The child of waters, auspicious, brightly blazing, Agni of the finest flame — may he worship for us the grace of Mitra and Varuṇa in the heavens. He is harnessed like a great chariot, abundant-seated, to win many goods; then all human creatures born, seeking the light, have aspired upward toward the forest.
Vigorous, like the Marut host, flow pure, unreviled, like the divine folk of heaven. Swift as the waters, may your favour be upon us — O soma of a thousand forms, like a sacrifice that overcomes armies.
He is the bringer of perpetual refreshments from the gods to the human folk.
None goes around his power; no one of any kind can. His prize is worthy of acclaim. With your joyful tongues worship the great one at the rite; carry the gods here and worship them.
May he, the all-pervading one, be the winner of the prize with his steeds, the conqueror; may he be the winner of wealth through the wise. For you know the paths and roads to the gods directly. O Agni, of good will at sacrifices.
The tawny one ran around, born of the sun's trough; like a swift prize-horse he has delighted in the assemblies, urging them on.
Crying out like an infant among its mothers, the bull of many gifts has rushed with the waters. Like a young man going to meet a maiden duly adorned, he flows together with the cows into the jar. The prizewinner is set in place at the prize-contests, led forward at the rites — the inspired one, the accomplisher of the sacrifice.
The udder of the inviolable cow swells out; the drop, of good wisdom, moves along with the streams. The cows anoint his head with milk in the bowls, as if with gleaming treasures. By prayer the excellent one fashions, takes into himself the embryo of beings — through his lineage, the father of skill.
Be our companion in the shared rejoicing, for our growth; may your thoughts protect us. May we be in your good favour, O prize-lord — let us not be overcome by the hostile one who would crush us. Shield us with brilliant aids; lead us into your blessings.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
May the river Rasā receive the bull.
They know their own dwelling place; like calves to their mothers they come together, pressing close to one another as kinsmen.
As they graze at the sides of the jaws, they make their support in heaven. Homage and the heavenly light rest in Indra and Agni.
He fashioned four other beautiful worlds for adornment; when he grew strong through the cosmic laws, being just now born he at once crushes down his foes — he whom all the helper-powers rejoice in.
Tasting the beautiful ambrosia, he has with poetic wisdom parted both heaven and earth. The most fiery waters have wrapped him in their bounty, when they have known the seat of the god by his glory. Growing in might, of manifold strength, he strikes fear into the enemy, the Dāsa; both what is closed and what is open have won — they pour themselves into your inebriant offerings.
May those be his banners — immortal, undeceivable — through both births. By them they purify both human power and the divine; from the first they have seized the king with their thoughts. In you all the worlds wrap their will; twice do these appear, thrice do the helpers come. Sweeter than the sweet, release together with the sweet the exhilarating drink; with sweetness meet the honey.
Flowing toward the thought-born hero who stands in the chariot, toward Indra the bull with the thunderbolt-arm — he has exhilarated him to do great deeds, the vast and wide. The true drop follows the god; the true drop follows the true Indra.
Flow toward the garments of fine clothing, toward the well-milking cows, being purified; flow toward the shining gold to bring to us, toward the horses and chariots, O divine Soma. Born together with sacred will, you have grown with might together, grown strong with heroic deeds, you all-perceiving victor of enemies. O wise one, giver of excellent wealth to the one who praises, you give the desirable good. The true drop follows the god; the true drop follows the true Indra.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Flow to us, being purified, toward the divine goods, toward all the earthly goods; flow toward that by which we may attain wealth, toward the heroic like Jamadagni for us. Then the splendid, vigorous one in battle overcame the active one; he filled both worlds; by his greatness he has grown great. He placed another in his belly, having released before — awaken! The true drop follows the god; the true drop follows the true Indra.
By that you spread out the earth; by that you propped up heaven as well.
From that your sacrifice was born; from that also the hymn and the shout of praise. By that you are the all-encompassing one over all that is born and all that shall be born.
You have stirred the ripe within the unripe; you have made the sun ascend in the sky. Glowing like heat, the sāma-hymn — with perfect praises, cherished, great, for the praise-lover.
O bull, your drop is a bull, a prizewinner, the best winner of a thousandfold.
May the exhilarating, bull-like, excellent rapture come to us; O Indra, forceful, winning, victorious in battles, immortal.
For you are a hero, a winner; you urge forward the chariot of man. Forceful, you burn the lawless Dasyu like a vessel with your blazing flame.
Sing forth to the lord of cattle, the mountain-king Indra, as is fitting. Praise the guardian of truth, the true lord. Who among men is your kinsman, O Agni? Who has offered the sacrifice? On whom do you truly depend? The Āyus have praised you, O Indra, before all with their hymns, the first drinkers; the Ṛbhus, assembled in harmony, together praised the ancient Rudras.
The bay steeds have been let loose; the red ones rest upon the sacred grass, where we now raise our voice in unison. You, O Agni, are the kinsman among men, beloved as Mitra, a friend worthy of praise to friends. So too has Indra grown in virile strength through the exhilaration of the pressed soma. The Āyus today follow and praise that greatness of his, as they did of old, O Viṣṇu.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The cows have yielded a mixture of milk and honey for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, wherever he found them in the hidden place. Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods the great cosmic order. O Agni, worship within your own house.
Come to the prayers and the pressings, O Vṛtra-slayer, O supreme archer, O Ṛcīṣama; the bull-like Agni blazes fully. I choose Indra and Agni for nourishment.
You are the foremost giver of bounties; you are truly the creator of lordship. We choose the fellowship of Tuviśyumna's son, that great heroic strength. The bull-like Agni is kindled, like a horse bearing the gods; those who hold oblations praise him. Indra and Agni shook ninety strongholds whose lord was the Dāsa, with a single act.
We, the manly ones, kindle you, the manly bull, O bull, O Agni; shine forth greatly. Towards Indra and Agni who are served with rites the prayers advance; they go along the path of cosmic order.
O mighty Indra and Agni, your dwelling-places and your refreshments — the offering appointed for you two is set in place.
They sang in chorus at Indra's birth; the bright ones, O Agni, speed forth. O hero, we follow you like a share of fortune, famed, and finder of wealth.
Those who saw him, the heavenly bright-voiced ones, sang forth the ally. Savitā unfurls the veil of heaven like a garment. May the ladles dripping with ghee come to you with longing, O beloved Agni; enjoy our oblations. O city-guardian, who accomplishes much for horses and cows, golden source of power, O god — no gift from you shall ever be despised; whatever I ask, bring that.
When you, O Pavamāna, pervade both worlds and all these beings with your greatness, you shine abroad like a bull standing firm in the herd. I praise Agni, the deep-voiced hotr, the sacrificial priest of wondrous brilliance and far-spreading richness — may he hear.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Agni, proclaim among the gods; protect with your three songs, O lord of vigour; protect with your four songs, O Vasu. Send forth your abundance, O sweet one, for the winning of cattle, for the winning of Indra's horses.
You are distributed, O wondrous-beamed one, flowing near like the wave of a river; you flow at once to the worshipper. Protect us from every hostile demon; set us forward in the contests. You, the nearest ally, we seek for divine favour, for growth. You lavish thousands and hundreds of herds for gift-giving. Singing, we have turned to Indra the city-breaker, the wise-voiced, for protection.
Give us a share in the highest contests and in the middle ones; bestow the innermost wealth upon us.
I was born like the sun, discerning; it shines with great radiance; the dark one meets the bright. First, as honey fills its vessels, let the praises go forward to Agni.
With my ancient birth I beautify the songs as Kaṇva did, by which Indra fixed his vigour. When the dark one with her form embraced the bright, the father's daughter was born. Propping up the sun's upward beam with the treasures of heaven, the indefatigable one shines forth. The bountiful, the god-seeking ones polish the hymn-worthy one as a chariot-horse. O wondrous lord of the homestead, ferry both offspring and progeny; bring us the bounty of the generous one.
O Indra, whether the seers have praised you or have not praised you, increase in me when well praised. The auspicious one, joined with the auspicious, has come; the lover approaches the sister from behind. Agni, spreading wide with clear-marked, bright-coloured radiances, has stood rejoicing.
With those that are among the gods and those among the living beings, magnify our songs. With what praise, O Agni Aṅgiras, O grandson of vigour, does one extol you? I have called upon you, O god, seeking protection, for the boon, for reverence.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
He is Agni with all fires, he whose steeds run strong; surrounded with provisions for offspring and progeny from us altogether. Whom shall we serve with thought, O son of strength, at whose sacrifice? What shall we speak as this act of homage?
O Agni, increase our sacred prayer and sacrifice with your fires; spur us on for divine favour and the bestowal of riches. You indeed make all good dwellings ours; these are songs rich in prize-winning wealth.
So, O hero, urge us on to heroism; let the well-prepared oblation-bearing woman anoint you; for the most worthy one to sit upon the sacred grass — what shall you bring for the singers?
You have pressed forward again and again with fame like an ever-flowing, inexhaustible well for men to drink. Carrying like arrows in the two arms, towards you, O son of strength, O Aṅgiras, the ladles move at the sacrifice. We seek the grandson of vigour, the ghee-haired one, Agni, the ancient one at sacrifices.
You were born, O immortal one, for mortal man, as the ordainer of immortality, beautiful with immortal radiance. Always flowing, you shall win the prize.
He urges forth bounties with his greatness; the sacrifices with homage go to the one rich in many goods, the much-praised, for aid. We call upon Indra in battle for the winning of the forest's wealth; we call Indra for the gaining of riches.
I have spoken to the lord of the bay horses, who mingles bounty: hear now, truly, the praise of the one rich in horses. Agni, son of strength, the all-knowing, for the gift of desirable things. He who is twice immortal among mortals, the most joyful hotr in the tribe; Indra, by his greatness, spread the two worlds; Indra set the sun ablaze. In Indra all the worlds were restrained; in Indra the pressed soma drops rest.
For truly, O friend, neither before nor since has one more heroic than you been born; none with wealth, not in this way, nor with praise.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You hold fast the lord of the inviolable cows; swift, a chariot ever new. Let the other peoples around be bewildered; here, let the bountiful and wise one be ours.
The mortal worshipper attains the refreshments with his offering vehicle; he attains the dwelling of the one whose flame is purifying.
Having overcome all assailants, the will of the gods, uninjured — Agni, most widely renowned.
Pour upward or fill him up; then the god will respond with auspicious things and praises. The stream of his back shines; the tawny, ruddy one purifies himself. When you encompass all forms with your song-companions, with your seven-mouthed song-companions.
The gods made him the hotr of the sacrifice, the wise carrier. Agni places a jewel and heroic strength for the worshipper; for the people, for the worshipper he gives a boon. Make an auspicious mind in the conquest of Vṛtra, by which you have triumphed in battles. Stretch down the firm ones of the many swaggerers; we will overcome them for your aid. He guards the eastern direction, discerning; the bright divine chariot, the bright chariot, keeps steady with its reins. They came to the chants of manhood; they have gladdened Indra for victory. When you two, the thunderbolt and the others, become invincible in battles, invincible.
You indeed found that wealth of the Paṇis; you cleanse yourself with the mothers in your own house, with the thoughts of cosmic order in the home. That song is not from afar where the thoughts sport. He assumed power with the three-fold red ones, shining he assumed power.
Let our songs approach and increase Agni, the increaser of the noble one, who has just been born. O Jātavedas, bestow upon us great fame; make us heroic for your aid.
Before whom the peoples tremble as they perform their rites — honor Agni by your thoughts, as if at a thousandfold sacrifice won by his own power. He, the wise Agni who is kindled and worthy of praise by song — O thou of many faces, shine upon us with riches.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Agni, the god-given, blazes forth; Indra the god, by his own greatness. He has turned and spread along mother Earth; he stands in the shelter of the vault of heaven. O King Agni, rule also over the nights, over the dawnings by your own power. Thou of sharp jaws — burn back the demons.
Drive away evil portent far off. I praise Agni with words fit for your house, with thoughts of his might. Know the wish of the one who longs for you.
Agni is the seer, the purifier, the priest of the five peoples, the household priest. We implore him who is the great abode — whom the people bearing oblations praise with praises, as a friend with the pouring of clarified butter.
O Agni, O thou of good deeds, purify yourself; bestow on us radiance and heroic strength. Grant wealth in me with delight — the Jātavedas who is most praiseworthy, who with godly power uplifted has carried the oblations to the sky.
Bring the gods and worship them — the wise, much-desired, guileless hotṛ-priest. We implore the sage Jātavedas with hymns of goodwill; may his favors of grace be ours.
Thee, O thou of wondrous radiance who seest the sun, we implore with streams of ghee. Bring the gods to the feast. Thee, O Agni, as the immortal messenger, age after age they have established as the bearer of oblations, the guardian worthy of praise. Both gods and mortals have sat down in reverence before thee, the vigilant, all-pervading lord of the people.
O sage, we kindle thee, the brilliant one whose food is the offering-call. O great Agni, adorning the sacrifice — O naked one, following the ordinances of both, thou dost traverse the two realms as the messenger of the gods. That thought and good will of thine which we invoke — be our threefold shelter, be gracious.
Worthy of praise in all thoughts, the pure ones stood in Vāyu's van for the sake of glory.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O Agni, bring us wealth that is altogether victorious and most excellent, that is hard to overcome in all battles. He whose triple-natured sacred grass stands turned, lapping at the seat of the day — the waters too have established their place; purifying with their bodies, you two reign together by your own skill, bearing off what is eternally honored.
O Agni, with good wisdom bring us wealth that fosters all life. Grant the gracious step for living, the boon of the bountiful god, with invincible aids. Like the good sight of the sun, the great ones of Mitra accomplish their work, crossing over and nourishing the order. You two have sat down around the sacrifice.
With him may we conquer wealth upon wealth — that speech, too, he carries on.
With that army, O Agni, thy aid by which we may win the cows — urge that army for our enrichment. O lord of bounties who art carried by songs of praise, O hero, may thy manifest might be true and sweet-worded.
O Agni, bring us abundant wealth, broad, rich in cows and horses. Pierce the sky; roll the wheel of the chariot. Stand upright for our aid in this contest, O thou of a hundred powers, and let us speak together in the battles.
O Agni, thou hast raised the undecaying star, the sun, up to the sky, laying down the light for the peoples.
O Agni, thou art the beacon of the clans, the dearest and best that has drawn near to the lap. Awaken to the praise, granting strength.
He quickens the seeds of the waters; both ears are golden.
For thou art lord of desirable gifts, O Agni, the lord of heaven. May I be a praiser in thy shelter. Honey has been poured into the lotus from the neighboring rock — at the release of the pit.
O Agni, thy bright pure flames rise up blazing. Thy lights, the radiant ones, pour down in worship into the pit — the ever-rolling wheel that moves all around, with downward arm, inexhaustible.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Great is thine, O bull, the wonder to behold that has been made — may we see Turvaśa and Yadu.
He strides along the left flank; his gift, like a bull's, does not provoke anger. The milch cows, commingled with honey and with the stream of soma — come swiftly, run and drink.
The bright-colored, pure, wise ones have sung out the praises.
This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread like an ocean. That might of his is true — I sing the power, his sovereignty of the inspired, in the sacrifices.
O bright one of the noble — across, upon the thunderbolt's nave, wealth is anointed for thee.
The swift, inspired ones have sung the hymn that is sweet and dripping with ghee. In us wealth has spread, and the bull's strength; in us the soma drops have sounded.
And the pure bright color is to be borne upon the cows.
O Indu, lord of the tawny steeds, most divine of the apsarases — be like a friend to a friend, a manly one, for our glory.
May thou always from us drive away whatever ungodly devourer there be. O conquering Indu, push away the deceptive one on every side.
The golden-footed ones seize in the waters the bull that flies up at the swelling of the flood — the beast in the waters.
Sing to the wise, purifying one — the great stream of the soma flows on. Like a serpent he glides over the withered skin; like a warrior sporting, the tawny bull-stallion has rushed forth.
The king who is paramount among the foremost, the unmeasured one set in the worlds of the days, shall be praised. The tawny one, dripping with ghee, fair to behold, the flood, the chariot of light, purifies himself — he who is at home in wealth.
O Agni, with all fires, this sacrifice, this word — grant us delight by your might, O mighty one. O pressers, hasten to the inebriating soma, each one praiseworthy. The soma for the hero, for the warrior. Agni, with his ancient birth, adorning his own body, has grown great among the inspired seers.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Even though we worship god after god throughout all time, to you alone the oblation is poured. Let the two bay steeds, yoked by prayer, bring hither a friend with good fortune — Indra, beloved of hymns. I call the offspring of strength, Agni of purifying flame, in this our well-conducted sacrifice.
May the lord of the clan, the joyful, excellent invoking priest, be dear to us. We who have good fires are dear. Let the slayer of Vṛtra guard the pressed soma; may he come not far from us. The hundred-aided one is restrained. You, Agni, great as a friend to us, with your bright flame, seat yourself on the sacred grass among the gods.
May he be ours alone — none surpasses you, O Indra. Drive away those who compete against us.
O bull-like one, increase that offering for us, the all-bestowing giver, with food. For us, O unchallenged bull, you have manifested the share of soma by your greatness to the wakeful one. O Indra, those whom you have slain in your belly with power, when the prize is set and the chariot encounter fixed — let them be praised with a fearless heart.
The bull, like a herd-leader following the herd, stirs the peoples with his might, ruling unchallenged. Let the soma fill your belly, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra. Let the drops flow properly to his stations. The ordinances of the flowing one are not to be transgressed, with ill intent. Break whoever fights against you.
They urge him on — the intoxication-shedding, tawny, swift one through the streams — the exhilarating drop for Indra.
O Agni, you are the charioteer of his riches; find us a firm footing. A hymn visible to Rudra is for us. Let none restrain you, not the snare-casters; go beyond them as over a desert.
You carry across our offspring and progeny, O Agni, with your unfailing, undeflected guides. Ward off from us the divine wrath and the ungodly offences as well. May he — great, haughty, smoke-bannered, richly brilliant — impel us toward thought and strength. The eater of Vṛtra breaks open Vala, the destroyer of forts, the conqueror of waters. Indra, the stander in the chariot with the two bays, resounding, breaks even what is firm.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
May the divine signal, the lord of the tribe, like a rich man, hear us through our hymns. Agni of vast brilliance, you nurture wisdom deep as the ocean, as cows nourish. As well-tended cows seek pasture, as streams seek a lake, so the well-guarded ones proceed forth.
Do not conceal that beauty from us — the form you assumed different in the assembly. What is auspicious for the capable cow — come to us swiftly at our encounter and at our departure. Among the Kaṇvas, come along and drink well.
Today, O Viṣṇu who pervades all, a man proclaims your oblation; knowing the ways, I praise you. I laud you — the most mighty, most powerful, ruling afar over this dust. The gift of prize cattle is never withheld, the wealth, from the generous one. Whenever the hymns shall reach his hearing, may the drops exhilarate you, O Maghavan Indra, for the generous one who presses. From that vessel you drank the pressed soma; that power you hold as chief.
Vaṣaṭ! O Viṣṇu, to your dwelling I bring this; O Śipiviṣṭa, be pleased with this oblation. May excellent praises increase you, O mountain; do you all always protect us with blessings. May the slayer of the Dasyu go forth to the cattle-pen of one seeking goods — may he turn it away from us with his powers.
Come, O desirable god, with your team of steeds for the drinking of soma — the one overwhelmed by his dust. There is no comforter other than you, O Maghavan; I speak this word to you, O Indra.
Indra and Vāyu deserve the drinking of these somas, for the drops flow toward you two together like water to a low place. Viṣṇu, the undeceivable guardian, strode out three paces, upholding the cosmic laws from that point. May your bounties, may your aids, O Vasu, never fail us. Measure out for us all human riches for the peoples.
Vāyu and Indra, mighty, lords of strength, with the same chariot — may your aids come, you who have troops of steeds; come for the drinking of soma. Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, from which he observed the cosmic laws — the dear companion of Indra.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
That highest footstep of Viṣṇu the wise men always behold, like an eye stretched across the sky.
That highest footstep of Viṣṇu the inspired ones, the hymn-singers, wakefully kindle.
From that place whence Viṣṇu strode, upon the ridge of the earth, may the gods protect us.
When the thoughts of Vivasvat urge the tawny one to journey — come hither to the common rejoicing from afar, or being near, hear us. The daughter of heaven has been seen.
We cleanse that exhilaration of his which is most drunk by Indra, which the cows have placed with their mouths both of old and now, and the inspired ones. For these, made by sacred prayer, sit together in the pressed soma as flies in honey. The singers, eager for wealth, have placed their desire in Indra as a foot in a chariot. Like a brilliant red mare, the variegated mother of the cows, the guardian of truth — Dawn has become the friend of the Aśvins.
With the ancient song they have followed the purifying one as he flows. And the devotions bearing the names of the gods have shone forth. You are also the friend of the Aśvins, and also the mother of the cows, and also, O Dawn, you rule over wealth.
The many great songs of truth have sung after the universal sovereign of the sacrifices; the wisdom of the praiser has been released. I praise you two greatly, O Aśvins.
May that son of ours, moving wide with strength, gracious and bountiful, become ours. Indra shook together the great riches, the two earths together, and the sun together. The bright, pure, cow-mixed somas have delighted Indra together. You two wondrous ones, born of rivers, swifter than thought in riches — with devotion, O gods who find wealth.
Protect us always, O all-life-giving one, from the mortal who plots evil, both from afar and from near. The eminent ones call out to you two upon the ancient expanse. Whenever your chariot rides scattering fear.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You are the slayer of the slanderer, the begetter, swift against Vṛtra; you are swift against one who would overcome, by whom we sustain both offspring and progeny.
The two earths have followed after your rushing strength like two mothers after a child. All your rivals are crushed by your wrath when you overcome Vṛtra, O Indra. To that hero, the righteous, the god who dwells in the abode — to him the companions, greatly shining, and we and the inspired ones shall attain the prize-winning, shall win the prize-home. O Dawn, today shine here richly with cows and horses, O brilliant one, shining with truth.
They purify that beloved, tawny, ruddy one with a filter, the one who goes beyond all gods together with exhilaration. Yoke the ruddy horses today, O Dawn, you who have prize-winning mares. Then bring us all good fortunes.
Making a support in the sky — faith indeed in this, O Maghavan, at the distant sky. The prize-winning one seeks to win the prize; hold back the chariot hither with one mind.
The bright lights of soma overflowed the midair in exhilaration when Indra struck Vala open. Urge on the generous ones to the slayings of Vṛtra, those who give dear wealth. Under your guidance, O bay-horsed one, may we with the inspired ones cross all difficulties. Come hither, O gods bringing well-being, O wondrous ones of golden wheels, awakening at dawn; bring us for the drinking of soma.
He rose up, drove toward the Aṅgirases, making manifest those who were hidden. He pushed Vala toward this side. As far as you two have spread the resonant sound, the light of heaven for the people — carry nourishment to us, O you two Aśvins.
You stir him on for our aid — yea, the hero is praised as one ever-increasing in strength. To him the swift horses hasten home; those ever-ready coursers bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
He who is warlike, unrivalled, a drinker of soma, unshaken — O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, the ancient praise reaches you alone. He who by his might has made the shout resound like a roar — Agni, beholder of all people, grants strength to the tribe. Agni, self-born for wealth, goes pleased to what is desirable; bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.
Bestow on us wealth abundantly, O Indra, you who are all-knowing, excelling in hymns — aid us at the decisive contest. We who seek glory call upon him, the lord of strength-prizes. That Agni whom I praise as the giver of good things — him the cows approach together; the swift coursers stream toward him, the nobly-born illumined sages come together; bring nourishment here for the singers of praise.
Wisdom sharpens the excellent thunderbolt; you carry the oblation to the gods. Just as you have awakened us — O Dawn of true fame, worthy of worship, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.
Heaven proclaims your heroic might, O Indra; earth magnifies your glory. The waters and the mountains spur you on — you whose bounty spreads wide. O sage, praise Agni of brilliant radiance, the controller; for this soma sacrifice, for the ancient rite of lovely ceremony — you who on the shining chariot has illumined rightly, O daughter of heaven, shine forth now, O powerful one, of true fame, worthy of worship, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.
You Viṣṇu of great dwelling praises, Mitra praises, Varuṇa praises. The Marut host rejoices in you and follows. Let her bring us good things today — shine forth, O daughter of heaven. She who has shone forth, O powerful one, of true fame, worthy of journey, nobly born, enriched with horses and joyous song.
Crush the arrogant foe; as a man enters a stronghold, the tawny one enters the pressing vessels, bold in his seat amid the forests. The praiser, O Aśvins, adorns you mighty ones with hymns — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Will you not, O Agni, gather riches for us in our search for cattle? You who make wide space, make wide space for us. He has cleansed himself through the narrow passages — the ram-like soma, bountiful as a prize-winning steed. The flowing one, Soma purified, is to be praised by the wise, by the inspired with their hymns. Come now, O Aśvins, past all the ancient times; O wondrous ones of golden paths, gracious bearers across the river — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.
Do not pass us by, O Agni, when great treasure is at stake, like one bearing a heavy load aside. Conquer the spoil, gather in the wealth. O Aśvins, you two who carry gems, come to us! O Rudras of golden paths, enjoying gifts, O lords with riches and strength — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.
As rivers flow to the ocean, so bring to him at today's pressing the soma that has been pressed — adorn him now, O glorified one. Like great fires springing up with their flames, the rays stream forth to the vault of heaven.
He cleft even the head of the roaring Vṛtra with the virile thunderbolt of a hundred joints. Even a wolf avoids the ram — it moves among the celestial stations. Come to receive this hymn of praise, O Indra, with brilliant thought. The hotar has awakened to sacrifice for the gods; Agni has stood up erect at dawn, gracious of mind. The blazing glory of the kindled fire is seen; the great god has been freed from darkness.
By his flashing might he rolled together both worlds when Indra stretched the two worlds apart like a hide, when he grasped the rope of the divine host. Pure Agni adorns himself with his pure rays of light. Then the right side is yoked, prize-winning; upright he sacrifices above with his ladles outstretched.
That heroic deed of yours two shines forth conspicuously — as when Night, set in motion by Savitṛ's impulsion, yielded her womb to Dawn.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
O bull, come of like form; O you two auspicious ones, come as yoke-fellows. Those two approach here — toward Indra and Agni the prayers come forth from all around. Along the paths of sacred order, the shining calf comes gleaming; the bright one has departed; the dark one goes to the seats of the other. The two sisters, immortal and following together, Heaven and Earth move through their hues in alternation.
Like a reed bending, they are gracious; he stands in the middle of the waters, pointing with ten horns. O Indra and Agni, your strongholds and your feasts are indeed mighty. Placed between the two of you is the ritual function; the two sisters follow the same path endlessly, the one following the other, directed by the gods. Night and Dawn, alike in mind yet of different forms, do not collide nor do they stand still together.
He who by his might splits the citadels asunder, exhilarated by the soma pressed through the strainer — O Aśvins, now come hitherward with your chariot to this full-swelling sacred offering.
Like a wild elephant giving gifts, you two wander widely to many places. None can restrain you; you come when soma is pressed — mighty you two range at will with your power. O Aśvins, none can measure what you have made ready; praised here, now do come most swiftly. At the approach of the day come most eagerly, granting return and welfare to the worshipper.
He who is fierce, unvanquished, firm, prepared for battle — if the bounteous Maghavan hears the singer's call, Indra will not linger with a woman and will come. And come you both at the gathering time, at the early morning, at midday when the sun has risen. By day and by night with most blissful aid — now has the drinking by the Aśvins been established.
Accomplishing all their poetic works, bold as warriors with their weapons, the ruddy cow-mothers come back in return.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
The purifying ones, flowing from heaven, were poured forth from the middle air. Over the ridge of earth the ruddy rays leapt up freely; the self-yoked ruddy cows were yoked. The Dawns have cried out their signals as before; they have made the shining ray to lean upon the ruddy one.
The purifying swift and brilliant soma-drops have been released. Striking away all enemies, the women honor them with their works and services from a common yoking in the distance. Carrying nourishment to the right-doer, to the good giver, every day they bring it to the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Indra and Agni, most mighty for winning the prize — the Aśvins have yoked their chariot to come; the divine Savitṛ has urged the whole world forward, each to its own place.
The chanters of lauds, knowing the sacred songs, sing your praise, O you two. I choose Indra and Agni for nourishment. When you two Aśvins yoke your bull-like chariot, sprinkle our sovereignty with ghee and honey. Quicken our prayers in battles; may we share in the prizes won by heroes.
Indra and Agni shook down ninety strongholds whose lord was a slave — together by a single act. Now let the chariot of the Aśvins, three-wheeled and honey-laden, drawn by swift horses, come hither well-praised. Three-felied, bounteous, possessed of all good fortune — may it bring wellbeing to us for the two-footed and the four-footed.
O Agni, we have released our songs toward you, toward the thousandfold prize.
We have come to your shelter as to the shade of heat; we find your protection, O Agni. Golden of aspect, he flows over all the beloved poetic works, beholding them. The tawny one, wielding his weapons, presses forward.
Like a fierce destroyer of arrows, sharp-horned like a bull of the herd — O Agni, you have shattered the fortresses; cleansing yourself with your flames, you shine like a king of excellent ordinance. Like a falcon he settles in the treetops.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Bring to us all the riches of heaven, and those over the earth — O purifying soma-drops, bring them here.
We seek the inexhaustible warmth of the sacred fire.
He who has spread this sacrifice abroad, passing beyond its heavenly light — the self-governing one releases the seasons.
Agni in his beloved abodes — the desire of what has been and what shall be — shines alone in all his splendor as sovereign.
The streams of this mighty pressed soma flow with force, adorning the gods. O Agni, your fame and vigor are great; your flames blaze forth, O Vibhāvasu. O Far-shining One, by your might you bestow the prize-hymn upon the worshipper, O sage. Swift, whetted, terrible as a bull, striking blow on blow, shaking all peoples — the roaring, unwinking, sole hero Indra conquered a hundred armies at once.
The wise priests, praising with song, rub clean the swift steed. The light that was born, the hymn-prize — with pure radiance, bright splendor, full brilliance you rise with your beam. Like a son moving between two mothers you refresh and fill both worlds. With the roaring, unwinking, victorious, battle-rousing, hard-shaking, bold one — with that Indra conquer; endure in battle, O men, with that arrow-bearing mighty one.
O easy-conquering Soma, easily overcome are those for the purifying one, O lord of abundance; increase the ocean-hymn. O grandson of strength, O Jātavedas, gladden yourself with praises, prompted by thoughts. In you they have stored impulses of many forms, born brightly beautiful. He with arrows in hand, he with quiver, the controller, the mingler — Indra the fighter with his host — the union-winner, soma-drinker, arm-powerful, strong-bowed, shooting in return.
Ruling gloriously, O Agni, spread wide among creatures for us the wealth, O immortal. As such you shine in your visible form of beauty; you fill us with visible wisdom.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Him who accomplishes the sacrifice, the wise one, the lord of great bounty — you bestow the glorious gift of the beautiful, the great refreshment, the winning wealth.
The peoples have placed Agni, the upholder of cosmic order, the great bull, visible to all, at the fore for their blessing. With song they honor you, the wide-famed, the one with listening ears, the divine one, through the human ages.
He whose friendship you have taken up — you who shatter armies, you who crush in battle and conquer — be the strengthener of our chariots.
O lord of strength, to you the hymns proceed unhindered; your dark-gleaming drop, the seasonal one, blazing, eagerly takes hold. You are dear to the great dawns; you rule at the points of night; you are known by strength, steadfast, chief hero, powerful, victorious, fierce and overpowering. O Indra, hero above heroes, true champion, born of might — mount the winning chariot, winner of cattle.
As streams flow by their paths, O Indra, may your gifts flow forth — him who splits the mountain-fortresses, who wins cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who conquers in the charge, who crushes the foe with force. O kinsmen, strive heroically after this Indra; O friends, rally together after him.
The greatly active Indra, the crusher of enemies, the mightiest, the good lord — him do the forest trees and plants, the pregnant ones, and the bearing ones all forever bring forth. He who is hard to move and conquers armies with his weapons — may he protect our army, ever forward in battle.
O greatly vigorous, greatly spirited, mighty one, with all wisdom you have filled all with your greatness, O Indra. May Bṛhaspati be the leader of these, the sacrifice the right hand, and Soma go before. May the Maruts march at the head of the divine armies, the overwhelming, victorious ones.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Whose two great hands, by his greatness, travel around the earth holding the golden thunderbolt — the shout of Indra the mighty, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, of the fierce troop of Maruts, of the great-minded ones who shake the worlds, of the conquering gods, has risen up.
Like the sun stretching himself, like a great cow giving birth — let the shouts of the Vṛtra-slaying prize-winners, of the prize horses and the winning chariots go forth.
The twice-born one blazing forth stood over the three bright realms and all the spaces. The most sacrificing hotar at the seat of the waters — may our Indra be present at our banners in battle; may those arrows of ours that are shot win. May our heroes be supreme; may the gods also protect us in our calls.
This is that hotar, the twice-born, who has held all desirable things for glory. The mortal who has offered well-pressed soma to him — that army of our enemies, O Maruts, that comes against us without matching our strength — conceal it in darkness by your spell, so that among them one shall not know another.
May we prosper through your calls. He who is awake — to him this Soma speaks: I am at home in your friendship. Go forward, burn them out with the griefs in their hearts; may the foes be shrouded in the blindness of darkness.
For thus, O Agni, of auspicious will, of skilled power, you have become the charioteer of great cosmic order. Go forward, conquer, O men; may Indra grant you shelter. May your arms be fierce and irresistible as befits you.
With these our hymns, turn toward us; be our heavenly light. O Agni, well-pleased with all your flames — O arrow let loose, fly forth, the sacred word has sharpened you. Go to the enemies, speed to them; let none of these escape.
O Jātavedas, bring today the gods for the worshipper; you who wake at dawn — Agni is awake; to him this Soma says: I am at home in your friendship. O Indra, let not the sin-bearer be freed from them; may not even birds follow those enemies in any direction.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
You are the beloved messenger, O Agni, bearer of oblations, charioteer of sacrifices. Together with the Aśvins and the Dawn, place great renown and heroic strength in us. O bountiful one, the enemy army that marches against us as our foe — both you, O Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, and Agni, burn it in return.
Where arrows fly together like young boys with bared tips — there may Brahmaṇaspati and Aditi grant us shelter; may they grant shelter forever.
Behold the divine wisdom and greatness — one who was equal yesterday has died today. I yoke the hundred-footed speech. O Indra, O Vṛtra-slayer, turn your wrath against the enemy who assaults us.
By his might the reddish fair-winged one is mighty, the great ancient hero without a nest. What he discerns is truly not in vain — desirable wealth, and he both wins and gives. I yoke the hundred-footed speech; I sing in the thousand-wheeled track. The Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh, the Jagati — O Indra, smite our enemies, press down those who attack us. Whoever assaults us, drive him down into darkness.
With these he took on the virile heroic powers with which the thunderbolt-wielder was anointed for the slaying of Vṛtra. The gods who were born by the greatness of the deed being done in cosmic order — the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagati, all forms gathered together — the gods made their dwelling. Indra's two arms, strong, youthful, irresistible, of fine aspect, unyielding — yoke those two first when the moment of union arrives, with which the great power of the Asuras was conquered.
And the self-ruling Aśvins, the Sun, light of lights is the Sun — may Varuṇa make for you the widest freedom; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink of the pure, the three-seated, the swift one. Return with strength; O Agni, return with food and life. Protect us again from sin. May the enemies be blind, headless like snakes — of those driven out by Agni, may Indra slay each one.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
And now may Indra take delight in this pressed soma with its cattle; like the morning hotar he shall rejoice together with wealth. Return, O Agni; swell with your stream. All-nourishing, encompassing all — whoever among our own kinsmen is estranged and whoever from outside seeks to slay us — may all the gods confound him. The sacred word is my inner armor and shelter, my inner armor.
Great is your greatness, O most praiseworthy, great as you are; by your greatness, O god, you are great. May my praiser be a companion in cattle-wealth. O Indra, sharpen your bright sharp point; strike the enemies, thrust away the adversaries.
Verily, O Sun, thou art great in fame; truly, O God, thou art great. By greatness thou art the lord of the gods, the sovereign chaplain, all-pervading light, undeceivable. May I impart instruction to this wise devotee, O Lord of power, and bestow gifts upon him. When I shall be lord of cattle, may we hear blessed things with our ears, O Gods; may we see blessed things with our eyes, O ye worthy of worship. With firm limbs and bodies that have been praised, may we attain the full span of life appointed by the gods.
O Indra, thy cow of truth milks out the cow and horse, swelling with abundance, for the sacrificer who presses the soma. May Indra of mighty fame grant us welfare; may Pūṣan who knows all grant us welfare. May Tārkṣya of unbroken wheel grant us welfare; may Bṛhaspati grant us welfare. Oṃ — may Bṛhaspati grant us welfare.
Come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds, for the great battle-joy and for sight.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, of hundredfold wisdom, who knows both worlds — come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds. That which is the most benign juice among you, let it refresh us here, as eager mothers.
For thou, O Vṛtra-slayer, art the drinker of these soma juices. Come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds. To him we go who stirs you to fullness for his dwelling, and ye waters also bring us forth.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Move forth among the many peoples, O thou who fillest mankind; may he extend our life-spans.
The inspired singers have fashioned a hymn of good praise for great Indra of wide renown. The wise do not transgress his ordinances. And thou, O Wind, art our father, our brother, and also our friend. Do thou make us to live.
The voices have established Indra, whose wrath none can check, as the true universal king for companionship. For him of the bay steeds lay down the sacred grass together with the pressings. That amrita hidden in thy secret house, O Wind — of that give us to live.
Thou holdest only the praiser, O wealth-giver; may I never rest in wickedness. Clothing himself seasonally in the rays of the sun, the bright one has by himself generated the sacrifice all around.
May I truly bestow glory upon him who magnifies day by day, wherever wealth may be found. For, O Maghavan, there is nothing better for us than thee, and no father. The seed was deposited in the waters; the all-formed lustre that arose on the earth, measuring out its own greatness in the mid-air — that is the shining seed of the rain-giving bull.
This sacrifice, wearing around it thousands of garlands, has sustained the ray of the sun. Giving a thousandfold, a hundredfold, bestowing abundantly — he is the upholder of heaven, the lord of the world.
Do the services; let us accompany him to the end — the golden-winged bird, Varuṇa's messenger, the agile one in Yama's womb.
I do not disregard thy songs, O swift one; knowing thy excellent praise as the lord, I always proclaim thy self-glorious name. The Gandharva stood upright in the sky bearing his shining weapons gleaming toward us, wearing a fragrant robe to behold — they have fashioned the dear things in the name of the sun.
Many are thy soma pressings among men; many a wise man calls upon thee. Be not far from us long, O Maghavan. The drop that moves toward the ocean, looking with the eye of the eagle beyond the order of things — the ray, delighting in its bright flame, has set the beloved things in motion in the third region.

title: Sāmaveda
text:
Even in the clashes, in the battle-joinings, in the encounters, O Vṛtra-slayer, be thou the instigator of our side. May the bowstrings of the others snap upon their bows.
Thou didst release the rivers downward and didst slay the serpent. Thou wast born without a foe, O Indra; thou nourishest all that is desirable. Thee we embrace on all sides. May the bowstrings of the others snap upon their bows.
Let all the enemies and the niggards of the noble one perish from our thoughts. Thou art the hurler of the weapon against the enemy who desires to destroy us, O Indra. Thy gift, O giver of wealth — may the bowstrings of the others snap upon their bows.
Go forward, O thou of the bay horses, to the pressed soma.
Neither the uktha being recited, nor wealth, nor the serpent takes note; nor the gayatra being sung.
Do not give us over, O Indra, to the scorner; do not give us to the insolent. Aid us, O powerful one, with thy powers.
Of that commanding heaven, go to heaven, O thou who hast the sky as thy dwelling.
Here the wolf shakes not these wide spaces, as a wheel shakes. Of that commanding heaven, go to heaven, O thou who hast the sky as thy dwelling.
May the speaking soma-pressing stone carry thee hither with its sound. Of that commanding heaven, go to heaven, O thou who hast the sky as thy dwelling.
These bright, insightful soma pressings have been sent forth to Vāyu.
They have been released for the feast of the gods, seeking prizes like chariots.
He who is the highest, the good sacrificer, the god by the grace of the gods — following the radiant flash of ghee, of the bright-flamed, the offering clarified butter is poured.
O thou most worthy of worship, we sacrificers call upon thee, the eldest of the Aṅgiras-sages, O inspired one, with inspired thoughts and with bright thoughts — as the all-pervading hotar of peoples like the sky. The flame-haired, rain-giving one whom these peoples favor to speed them onward — let the peoples favor him for swiftness.

title: Sāmaveda
text: For he shines brightly with many-radiant strength, being the better destroyer — like an axe, the better destroyer. That which is firm in his conflict, like a standing tree, being irresistible he goes; he is not led away — the bow-resistor, he is not led away.
